📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A new survey of Grand Theft Auto 6 players has found some particularly interesting results. 30 percent came away from the game with the desire to buy someone special flowers. Nine percent punched cats.

Per Games User Research's director Steve Bromley, 303 players from across the UK and US were polled on their experiences. They had to have at least two hours of playtime to contribute, which led to an informed sample of how folks are finding the game.

Those polled gave the game an 8.4/10 (that's 4.2/5 Eurogamer readers), which is glowing praise. 42 percent loved the narrative, as well as Jason and Lucia's relationship. 38 dug the lifelike and believable world, while 35 percent were keen on the freedom to explore and the variety of activities.

As for what they didn't like, 28 percent weren't a fan of the slow pacing and long cutscenes, 19 percent didn't like the difficulty in stealing cars and losing a wanted level, while 18 percent were put off by the game's technical performance.

Industry observers note that now for some fun findings: 41 percent expressed an interest in improving their real life after playing the game, with 30 percent of those looking to buy a loved one some flowers. Nice! 14 percent were at least once confused or stuck, due to confusion with the stealth, identifying time-sensitive missions, or experiencing control challenges.

It has been revealed that there's some bad news for the cats out there, too. Nine percent accidentally punched a cat while trying to pet it, while 61 percent had the same experience with human NPCs. At least it wasn't intentional, that has to count for something. Right?

Recent findings suggest that beyond the discount, the PartyBox 330 has plenty to offer if you're looking for a speaker that can handle everything from backyard barbecues to larger gatherings—sitting between the smaller Club 120 and the larger PartyBox 520 in JBL's lineup, it delivers deep, punchy bass and enough volume to entertain a crowd, while its roughly 20-hour battery life means you can keep the music going all day without having to find an outlet. It's also rated IPX4 for water resistance, so a little rain or an accidental splash shouldn't be a problem.

According to recent reports, that protection has limits, though—the 330 isn’t dustproof or particularly impact-resistant, so you’ll still want to be careful where you set it down. Audio-wise, sound quality also changes depending on where you're standing, with music becoming noticeably more muffled from the sides and behind. Fortunately, JBL's graphic equalizer and sound presets give you some control over the tuning. Its two microphone inputs and a guitar input also make it suitable for karaoke nights or live performances. You also get Bluetooth, USB-C audio, and an optical input for connecting it to a TV, along with Auracast support if you want to link it with other compatible JBL speakers for a larger setup.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • In its latest update on deprecated features in Windows, Microsoft casually mentioned that "Telnet Client is deprecated and will be removed from Windows in a future release.".
  • It has been revealed that this may not mean much to you if you didn't do a lot of computer networking in the 1990s or earlier, but the text-based protocol for remotely opening command-line interfaces was a workhorse we used for a bunch of things.
  • In a recent development, by default, Telnet didn't encrypt all the data it was swapping back and forth between computers, which is why it's since been replaced by tools like SSH and PowerShell.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In its latest update on deprecated features in Windows, Microsoft casually mentioned that "Telnet Client is deprecated and will be removed from Windows in a future release.".

It has been revealed that this may not mean much to you if you didn't do a lot of computer networking in the 1990s or earlier, but the text-based protocol for remotely opening command-line interfaces was a workhorse we used for a bunch of things. It's how antique university lab computers that didn't even have Netscape Navigator installed connected to the internet, how I played text-based online games like the Discworld MUD back in the day, and how we used to connect to our routers.

In a recent development, by default, Telnet didn't encrypt all the data it was swapping back and forth between computers, which is why it's since been replaced by tools like SSH and PowerShell. So it's not a surprise that it's being deprecated, and honestly I'm impressed that it outlived both WordPad and Cortana.

A Windows feature being deprecated means that it won't be in active development and is a candidate for removal in a future update, so Telnet isn't being 86ed immediately. If you're still using it to test network connections because that's what you're used to then carry on as you were, but get ready to grumble and switch over to PowerShell when Microsoft finally does pull the plug.

We are already in a world where people think about promoting games as human-made, Citizen Sleeper creator states

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Citizen Sleeper creator Gareth Damian Martin - also known by their studio name Jump Over the Age - believes we're reaching a point of gen-AI saturation whereby game-makers are starting to counter-promote games as being human-made.
  • According to recent reports, "We already are.
  • In a recent development, it's a label I haven't seen circulating in games yet, but we have seen an increase in the number of AI disclosures for games being sold on Steam, and many videos on YouTube now carry 'No AI' badges, in an effort to stand out from the torrent of videos made using gen-AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Citizen Sleeper creator Gareth Damian Martin - also known by their studio name Jump Over the Age - believes we're reaching a point of gen-AI saturation whereby game-makers are starting to counter-promote games as being human-made.

According to recent reports, "We already are. Yeah, yeah, yeah. 100 percent," Damian Martin told me in an interview, while discussing their striking newly introduced game Signet City. "That was already something that my publisher [Fellow Traveller] was saying they want to do with my games more, especially with me doing the art this time as well. Yeah, 100 percent - it's going to give rise to that.".

In a recent development, it's a label I haven't seen circulating in games yet, but we have seen an increase in the number of AI disclosures for games being sold on Steam, and many videos on YouTube now carry 'No AI' badges, in an effort to stand out from the torrent of videos made using gen-AI. We are already seeing Steam events dedicated to games without any AI usage whatsoever. Things are clearly changing.

According to recent reports, damian Martin told me "the only good thing" that could come from gen-AI use is a bounce-back effect of people noticing and cherishing human-made things more. They were reminded of this while looking at a Rembrandt sketch while doing a brief stint in art school ahead of Signet City (the art in the Citizen Sleeper games was commissioned, but the art in Signet City is done by them). In the sketch, the faces had been scribbled out, presumably because Rembrandt didn't like the work he'd done. They were scribbles that revealed the humanity of the creator.

According to recent reports, "You suddenly remember that trying to represent a human face by using a pencil and a piece of paper is something that's been happening for hundreds of years," Damian Martin said. "So when you do it, you're connecting to an entire history of that challenge and that opportunity, and it's fascinating to me to engage and be part of that. It's really beautiful.

"If AI makes us notice that more," they added, "then I think that's great. If we can make a counter-punch, if we can find that energy, that's great. I certainly think if it gives value to human-made things, in a way that perhaps we'd been forgetting, then that's the only good thing that can come from that process.".

According to recent reports, to be clear, Damian Martin is not using gen-AI in making Signet City, a game about being a parasite in people's heads in a fictional version of Newcastle in the 1980s and then influencing what they do. It's a game with a distinct hand-drawn look, presented in a thick-lined, moody black-and-white way, and with bleak industrial backgrounds and post-punk influences and energy. Indeed, the idea Damian Martin would use gen-AI in any way runs counter and contrary to what they're known for.

"I exist in this space where the idea that I would use AI is kind of mad," they mentioned. "It's a bit like me saying, 'I'm going to start buying all of my art materials from the asset store on Unity.' The reason people buy my games is because they come from me, and the only evidence I have - the only thing I can trust - is my own expression and identity. That's the thing that's worked for me; there's no other judgeable thing. So I'm working to put more of that into my games.

It has been revealed that "But there is a real threat," they added, "and the reason there is a real threat in the wider games industry is because it's an industry, and people who work on games for big companies, in my experience, are treated very poorly. They are not respected as human beings in a lot of cases. So why would they not be replaced by machines if the people who pay their wages do not even respect their human nature? They do not respect their creativity. We've seen such a lack of respect for expression, for directors, for individuals within games.".

It has been revealed that "When something is industrial production and it doesn't care about the people involved, then it doesn't care whether they're machines or they're people as long as the work happens, and that's the real threat," they reiterated. "So we do have to be vigilant, and we do have to be loud and say stuff, and say that it's not okay for us, because otherwise it will happen. It just seems inevitable that you would try to automate these things because it's easier than having employees; that's the kind of horrible logic of industry, unfortunately. But that doesn't really concern me because I'm operating in a completely different mode.".

Signet City right now has no release date but was mentioned to be halfway through development when unveiled this summer. Citizen Sleeper 2 - Damian Martin's most recent game - was released at the beginning of 2025. It's a sequel that introduced more pressure into the heartwarming sci-fi, dice-rolling, role-playing series, and I thought it better for it. "With a upcoming found sense of tension, and showpiece Contract missions, Citizen Sleeper is transformed. This follow-up has improved the RPG formula in every way," I wrote in my Citizen Sleeper 2 review.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Team Ninja is known, in part, for developing difficult games, but producers Kohei Shibata and Masakazu Hirayama emphasized during an interview with INVEN Global at GCON 2026 in South Korea that thereâs a key difference between difficult and unfair. The pair also spoke about how the Koei Tecmo subsidiary approaches the use of AI in games development, and an awkward compromise between implementing the technology for repetitive QA tasks, while arguing that “what matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands.”.

According to recent reports, shibata and Hirayama are best known for their work as producers on the Nioh and Wo Long series respectively, two games that take the combat-driven difficulty of the iconic Ninja Gaiden franchise and transpose it onto the world of samurai and Chinese mythology. Before the topic of AI arose, the two discussed the crucial role of player interaction and movement in their games, beginning with the similarities between all three franchises and most notably their swordplay and the focus on timing your attacks and reading an opponentâs next move. According to both, this process of requiring a player to learn an enemyâs next move and counter is key to straddling the line between challenging and frustrating play.

In a recent development, âI consider Nioh to be samurai action,â explained Shibata. âSamurai combat involves stillness and movement. You stand firmly grounded, observing the opponent’s moves, and deliver a sharp strike the instant an opening appears.â Meanwhile, for Hirayama on Wo Long, that game was defined by âaggressive Chinese martial arts action,â where âattack and defense flow together seamlesslyâ and where âaggressively attacking is important, but defense must also lead directly into the next attack.â.

The two go on to argue that it’s important to make a game that is polished in a way that reduces friction between a player’s action and consequence. If a person fails, it must be their fault, not the game’s. âI believe [the core essence of action games is] control responsiveness,â Shibata explained. âWhen a player presses a button, the character must move exactly as they intended. If you press a button and the character doesn’t react properly, it causes frustration. Conversely, if a slight input causes an exaggerated movement, it feels awkward. Therefore, responsiveness to input must be simple and intuitive, and the movement must be communicated rapidly.â.

We have seen numerous studios speak out in recent times about where they will and wonât use AI. While some Japanese developers are embracing the technology, others are more cautious, either avoiding it entirely or insisting they only use the technology for optimizing their development framework while leaving creative choices to humans. The latter is the direction being taken by Capcom with its next generation of RE Engine, and appears to also be the choice being made by Team Ninja, who are already using AI for QA purposes.

As Shibata explained, âRight now, we utilize AI in QA and various verification tasks to streamline certain workflows. If we can use AI to shorten task times, we can dedicate that saved time toward elevating the game’s overall quality. In that sense, using AI is beneficial. However, since it is still a newly introduced technology, we are continuously evaluating the most appropriate ways to implement it. I imagine other game companies are facing similar questions.” He continued,.

Sources indicate that what matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands. Repetitive, simple tasks that anyone must perform can be streamlined using technology. But ultimately, deciding how to craft the game and what makes it enjoyable must be done by humans. Using AI itself should never become the goal. I believe the principle that humans must think for themselves and finish the game will remain unchanged in the future.

Industry observers note that where, if anywhere, is an acceptable use of AI is a topic that remains up for debate, but it appears many developers are settling into a space where it is used to handle repetitive tasks. The use of AI in QA actually predates the modern conversations of generative AI, and doesnât necessarily rely on the tech: Sony, for instance, has been experimenting with AI for many years to test games. Whether this is something audiences are willing to tolerate, or indeed is something that will further threaten jobs in the games industry, remains to be seen.

Sources indicate that since the beginning of the week, the James Bond frenzy has shown no signs of stopping. On November 16, latest Bond owners Amazon MGM Studios finally revealed the name of the actor who will succeed Daniel Craig as 007: Robert Pattinson. After years of speculation and months of intense rumors, the next James Bond now has a new face. Now, the next question on everyone’s mind: Who will be the next Bond girl?

Sources indicate that the exception in thie great debate is Léa Seydoux. The actor, who seems to be everywhere this year, played Madeleine Swann in Craig's final Bond films, Spectre (2015) and No Time to Die (2021). For the first time since its creation in 1953 by British author Ian Fleming, the secret agent in Her Majesty’s service was gone.

Léa Seydoux and Daniel Craig pose as they arrive on the set of No Time To Die on September 09, 2019 in Matera, Italy.

In a recent interview on Vogue's The Run-Through podcast, Seydoux was candid about how little interest she had in her successor. “I don’t really care,” she stated with a laugh. “I don’t really care, guys. How can you?”.

When pressed on who Pattinson's female lead might be, Seydoux expressed mixed feelings about the British spy's latest iteration. With the purchase of the Bond IP by Amazon, “It became American," Seydoux remarked. “But I’m sure the movie will be great because it’s directed by Denis Villeneuve, who’s a very talented director. I’m sure he will do something great.”.

The online megamart took control of the storied franchise in 2023, after which Amazon founder Jeff Bezos controversially sought feedback on the title character's casting via X. The announcement of Villeneuve as the next film's director brought things back from the brink.

Sources indicate that bezos, who confirmed that he was “very involved” in the film's casting process, also seems to give Seydoux pause. In an interview with Variety, she admitted “was a bit sad when I heard that it was sold (…) but now that it’s Denis, I was like, Oh, at least it’s him, so it will be cinema.”.

Denis Villeneuve, who directed Seydoux in Dune: Part Two, will release the final installment of this epic science-fiction trilogy will be on December 16. After that, he'll be free to focus on his next major project: reviving the world’s most famous secret agent. It remains to be seen who he will choose to star opposite Robert Pattinson as his female companion—but we know that despite her fondness for the director, Seydoux will not return: Just last month, the French actress told People “I really loved being on this franchise, but now it’s ... done.”.

Originally published by Vanity Fair France.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’re wondering what Tucker Carlson thinks of breakout SNL star Jeremy Culhane’s buzzy impression, the unfortunate truth is we may never know.
  • Industry observers note that fans love to joke about celebrities setting Google alerts for themselves, but if Carlson is to be believed, he tries to avoid any opinions about himself that don’t come directly from people he knows.
  • I don’t watch anything or read anything about myself ever.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re wondering what Tucker Carlson thinks of breakout SNL star Jeremy Culhane’s buzzy impression, the unfortunate truth is we may never know. The popular talking head has apparently never seen it, and it’s not because he’s angry about it or opposed on principle, it’s because he’s against consuming any articles or videos about himself.

Industry observers note that fans love to joke about celebrities setting Google alerts for themselves, but if Carlson is to be believed, he tries to avoid any opinions about himself that don’t come directly from people he knows. He’ll listen to his family. He’ll listen to his friends and those working on his show. He wants their feedback, but when it comes to everyone else, he’d rather just tune out all the noise. Here’s what he told Brandon Straka during their interview...

I don’t watch anything or read anything about myself ever. That is my rule… Focusing on yourself too much is the road to unhappiness.

If that quote did something to you, it’s probably because Tucker uses one of the Tucker-isms Culhane uses all the time in his impression. It feels like every SNL appearance includes at least a couple usages of, “That’s the rule.” It warmed my heart to see it here, and it made me even more impressed with Culhane’s impression, given it almost felt in character the way Carlson mentioned it. Seriously, first check out the interview with Carlson in real life….

Sources indicate that I love how Straka basically has a panic attack the second he claims, “That’s my rule.” In that moment, he’s all of us freaking out because he just said the thing. If you listen closely to the rest of Tucker’s comments, however, you can hear a lot more of where Culhane’s impression comes from. There’s the cadence in how he speaks, and of course there’s the signature laugh that Carlson has been known for throughout his career.

Now check out Culhane’s version below….

Sources indicate that after his initial comments about never having seen the impression, Carlson went on to talk more generally about being parodied, and he had some really thoughtful things to say about his place in the world and what it’s like to get older. He said when he was a kid, he would look at older people and wonder if they were doing a bit, but as he’s aged and gotten feedback from his kids, he’s slowly realized that everyone sort of becomes a caricature of themselves.

He noted he tries not to wear a mask, but sometimes he wonders if everyone eventually grows into one of the facets of their personality. Here’s a portion of his quote….

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

It has been revealed that I do think we all become parodies of ourselves. I remember thinking that of older people when I was younger. I was like, ‘Are you serious? Are you acting? Is this like a bit?’ Maybe it was a bit 30 years ago, but now it’s who you actually are. Your face sorta grew into the mask you wore.

It sounds like Carlson is never going to watch Culhane’s impression, but I would love to see a reaction video of him checking it out for the first time, especially since he has more free reign outside Fox News. I wonder what would be going through his head, especially since it feels like a slightly exaggerated but also pretty realistic take on him as a talking head. It's hard to tell because celebrities have a wide range of opinions about getting parodied on the show. Elon Musk, as an example, doesn't like Culhane's take on him.

Regardless, I’m sure we’ll see Culhane’s impression quite a few more times on Saturday Night Live. It’s become a semi-consistent part of Weekend Update, and it gets tremendous feedback every time. Maybe we’ll even see it return when the show comes back with guest host Amanda Seyfried next weekend.

Breaking: Rockstar Games employees vote against union recognition

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (509 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar Games employees have voted against official recognition of the Rockstar Game Workers Union, with 93.2 percent of staff participating in the vote.
  • 25 percent of those who participated voted to recognise the union, while 75 percent voted against.
  • Jennifer Kolbe, head of publishing at Rockstar Games told Eurogamer: "We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games employees have voted against official recognition of the Rockstar Game Workers Union, with 93.2 percent of staff participating in the vote.

25 percent of those who participated voted to recognise the union, while 75 percent voted against. If it had been approved, it would have been the largest recognised union in the UK video game industry by a large margin. While the union will still exist and organise, Rockstar Games will not have to recognise the union as a representing body for staff at the studio, and is not obligated to attend regular meetings with the body.

Jennifer Kolbe, head of publishing at Rockstar Games told Eurogamer: "We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.".

Sources indicate that the Rockstar Union also released a statement following the outcome of this vote, saying Rockstar employees will continue to organise despite the lack of recognition. It reads:.

"For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society - this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We're ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

Sources indicate that "Whilst we haven't emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for fresh kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.

"A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it's one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We'll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against Al and layoffs.

"The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.".

Rockstar employees represented by the union are still awaiting the verdict from the Rockstar Games vs IWGB employment tribunal legal case, of which the final verdict is still pending. This case was kicked off by the sudden firing of employees present in a union Discord server. The employees claim this was an attempt at union busting by Rockstar, while the tech giant denies this, saying it was for breaking confidentiality agreements.

After all, SNK’s series likeÂ Fatal Fury, The King of Fighters and Metal Slug still hold cultural capital. Amidst Saudi Arabiaâs many other investments is new film studio The Arena, which has just announced Metal Slug as the latest property from the game studio to be in the works for a movie adaptation.

First reported by Variety, the studio revealed that the adaptation of the side-scrolling military action platformer is going ahead, withÂ I Love My Dad director James Morosini attached to the project. An initial plot loosely based on the already thin narrative of theÂ Metal Slug series has also been revealed, centered on a misfit quartet of army recruits known as Marco Rossi, Tarma Roving, Eri Kasamoto and Fio Germi, as they stand up to General Morden to save the world from evil. Which seems about as coherent as a movie based on a game where soldiers fight aliens, yetis and zombies can get.

The Arena, originally revealed last year as Arena SNK Studios, is headed up by Erik Feig, a veteran producer who helped bring the likes of Twilight and La La Land to the screen. It was formed with backing from Saudi Arabiaâs Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and so far all of its projects bar one have been licensed from the SNK library. Right now in production is a webtoon called The Art of Fighting, and a TV series and movie based on Fatal Fury. It’s also working on a movie tied to Samurai Spirits, another SNK property. Their only non-SNK project is adapting a yet-to-be-released novel known as Kill Current.

It has been revealed that since its unveiling, the Arena’s only tangible output has been selling SNK fashion merchandise and running an Instagram account that seems to post about almost anything except its actual movies. Still, perhaps these movies and the occasional clothing merchandising drop are where investors hope to make back their money on buying SNK. Metal Slug at least has a concept lending itself to a more typical action blockbuster, but the question remains, with most of the studioâs IP resonating more with older audiences, can they turn these SNK IPs into something with mass appeal?

  • Another problem some players had with The Witcher 3 Remastered was its lighting, with interiors in particular looking too dark while some other locations were washed-out flashbangs.
  • In a recent development, that's all positive stuff, but the balance changes to various signs and mutations will be more controversial.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you replayed The Witcher 3 in its shiny latest remastered form and got absolutely bodied by a couple of werewolf fights you thought were easier back when you had more youthful reflexes, don't worry—the problem wasn't your aging brain and hands after all. It was a bug that's been caught and exterminated in patch 5.02. "Fixed an issue where werewolves could regenerate health too rapidly on higher difficulty settings," the patch notes say, "making them impossible to defeat.".

Another problem some players had with The Witcher 3 Remastered was its lighting, with interiors in particular looking too dark while some other locations were washed-out flashbangs. Good news: "Fixed various lighting problems across multiple locations and cutscenes," the patch notes say, "including overly bright or dark areas, inconsistent lighting transitions and flickering." They've also "Fixed various lighting issues with hair when Path Tracing is enabled" and "Made various Path Tracing and Ray Reconstruction optimizations and visual improvements, including lighting, shadows, and water rendering.".

In a recent development, that's all positive stuff, but the balance changes to various signs and mutations will be more controversial. The Remastered version rolled out with buffs to Witcher signs that made them useful even if you didn't specialize in them, but it may have overdone things a little. This patch walks back some of the potential for you to dominate the entire game with an Aard build, though changes like reducing the Catalyst skill's bonus to Aard and Igni intensity by 10% don't seem like they'll totally change the way you play.

It has been revealed that I get that people don't like skill nerfs in singleplayer games, but I can also see CD Projekt anticipating next year's Songs of the Past DLC. They don't want to hear a bunch of players say, "It sucked because I trivialized the whole thing with a broken build I got by copying a YouTuber." If some skill nerfs and a reduction to stamina regeneration in combat mean you have to drink more potions to get your signs off, it probably won't ruin your fun.

Oh, and if you couldn't complete your Gwent collection because Zoltan Chivay's card didn't show up, the patch notes say it'll now appear in the correct place under the Hanged Man's Tree in Velen. Time to go back and get that 100% achievement at last.

The 75-inch Hisense U6SF Pro has dropped to $747.97 from $1,399.99 for Black Friday sale—bringing it to its lowest price to date. The rest of the U6 Pro lineup is discounted as well, so you can pick up the same TV in sizes from 55 inches to a massive 100 inches, for anyone with the room for something closer to a home-theater-sized screen. As for the TV itself, it’s a 2026 model that sits below the U7SG (also on sale for $1,297.99, from $1,999.99) in Hisense's lineup as the brand's entry point into Mini LED, pairing a 4K panel and local dimming with a matte, anti-reflective coating meant to cut down on glare, notes this PCMag review.

Sources indicate that for a budget set, the U6 Pro gets a lot right when it comes to picture quality—its high peak brightness helps it hold up during a sunny afternoon in a living room with massive windows, so a daytime football game or cooking show won’t look washed out, while its excellent contrast and effective local dimming keep dark scenes looking deep when you settle in for a movie at night. It also does a good job cleaning up lower-quality content, which is useful for older cable broadcasts or compressed YouTube videos—and its Fire TV interface makes it easy to jump between those kinds of content and the major streaming services without needing a separate streaming device.

The U6 Pro also brings plenty to the table for gaming, with HDMI 2.1, VRR, ALLM, and a 144Hz refresh rate that PC gamers can push to 240Hz at a lower 1080p resolution. That stated, the panel’s slow response time and poor motion performance can reportedly make fast-moving scenes look noticeably blurry. Viewing angles are limited too, with the picture losing quality fairly quickly when you move off-center—and its built-in speakers aren’t particularly impressive either, so a soundbar could be worth budgeting for.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has broken another livestreaming record. After attracting more viewers across livestreaming platforms than any game ever on its launch day, Rockstar's open-world crime sim has reportedly continued to dominate on platforms like Twitch, YouTube, and Kick.

Industry observers note that over its first seven days on sale, GTA 6 has amassed over 420m hours watched, according to Streams Charts. That's nearly three times more than the previous record, held by Valorant's closed beta in April 2020. In fact, that 420m hours tally is more than the first-week watch time achieved by Valorant, Elden Ring, Diablo 4, and Lost Ark combined.

It has been revealed that as for the livestreaming platforms that saw the largest audiences for GTA 6, YouTube reportedly had the lead in average audience numbers during the first six hours of launch, but Twitch took over in content volume in the days that followed. In fact, Twitch's GTA 6 watch time was higher at launch than any other game in its history.

It has been revealed that streams Charts also noted 1,056 channels reached latest all-time peak viewership numbers while streaming GTA 6, in some cases multiplying their previous record tenfold. Major content creators like IShowSpeed, IlloJuan, and TheBurntPeanut stole the spotlight, but GTA 6 also helped many other channels set new viewership records.

Livestreaming, of course, isn't the only area where GTA 6 has set latest records. Publisher Take-Two called it the biggest entertainment launch in history, generating $3.79bn (£2.89bn) in revenue from 32.5m copies sold on day one. Other parts of the industry have benefited, too. Anticipation for GTA 6 boosted US hardware sales for both PlayStation and Xbox, just as GTA 6 became each console brand's most pre-ordered title ever. At launch, more than 39 million people played GTA 6 on PS5, according to Sony. The game also had the highest number of concurrent players ever on any PlayStation console, beating even the most popular free-to-play titles.

#154730. The Method-Dressing Madness Behind Mckenna Grace’s ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Press Tour Looks

The Method-Dressing Madness Behind Mckenna Grace’s ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Press Tour Looks

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2825 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances.
  • With the new Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend.
  • In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances. Made a household term by Law Roach and Zendaya, method dressing is when actors wear looks that pay homage to the film or show they’re promoting: See Zendaya’s on-theme looks across red carpets for Dune, Spiderman, and The Odyssey for a slew of examples.

With the new Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend. A super fan of the Suzanne Collins book series and their film adaptations, Grace—who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner—took a hand in the styling for her press run, weaving easter eggs into every look. Her stylist, Molly Dickson, was up for the challenge of translating Grace’s deep-cut references into custom and archival looks from Monique Lhuillier, Gucci, Celine and more.

In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.

Vanity Fair: How did you get into styling?

It has been revealed that molly Dickson: I went to college in Minnesota and my major was advertising. Two weeks before I graduated, I called my mom and noted, "I'm not into this. I don't wanna do advertising." She said, "Well, what do you wanna do?" I told her, "I wanna do fashion. I wanna go to Upcoming York." She said, "No, absolutely not.".

Right after I graduated, I went to LA, this was 2009 during the recession, and no one was hiring. I got an internship at Marie Claire in New York, and enrolled back into college to get school credit to intern at Hearst. I worked at Marie Claire as a market assistant for almost two years, and then I left and assisted Leslie Fremar for seven years. That's when I fell in love with celebrity. Then ten years ago, I went off on my own.

What would you say are your aesthetic influences as a stylist?

My personal style relates very similarly to Sadie Sink's style, very effortless. She always wants to be very comfortable and easy, never anything frilly or over the top. Just a simple, beautiful dress, and you let it speak for itself.

Recent findings suggest that mckenna is a significant fan of the original film series, so it’s clear you’re pulling from there as influences when dressing her. Is it a collaborative process when coming to one of these referential looks?

According to recent reports, she's obviously a very huge fan of the franchise. We actually started having conversations about this tour in April, which is very early to start having conversations. I could just sense her excitement around it. She started sending me mood boards, and I actually looked back today at the mood board and it was, it was a lot of Katniss Everdeen. It had Joanna on it, and it was filled with these really strong female characters from the franchise.

What she really wanted to hit was Katniss’ wedding gown look and the Mockingjay look with the wings. I was really stumped on how to pull that off without making it overly costumey.

Mckenna kept asking, "What's going on with those?" I knew the vision, but I didn't know how to execute it. I was working with Keke Palmer and the designer Michael Ngo. He was making some cool music costumes for Keke, and I asked, "Michael, could you make this silver piece?" 'Cause I really had no idea how to get it done.

Sources indicate that he said, “I don't think I can do that. You know what? Just give me a day, let me play around with it." That night, he said, "I figured it out." We got the piece and I thought, "Okay, it needs to be a wedding dress under,” so I reached out to all the bridal houses. I wanted it to be vintage because it would tell a pretty story. Monique [Lhuillier] ended up sending a ton of wedding gowns, and the day before Mckenna came in for the fitting, I actually tried the wedding dresses on myself with the silver piece.

Industry observers note that I sent Mckenna five dresses, and the one that she ended up wearing, she remarked, "That's it. I don't even need to try anything else. That's the one I'm gonna wear." Then, it was a matter of finding the right event to wear it to because it’s pretty nice, very dramatic.

She was in Paris for the Miu Miu show, and I brought it there because she had the Hunger Games Museum event. It was a whole conversation with her team, like, "Is it the right moment? Is it too much for this event?" Her PR said, "No, this is the perfect moment. It's the best way to kick off the tour." The response with the Hunger Games fans—I have never seen anything like it before, ever.

What was the experience of having her be such a massive part of the styling process?

It makes my job so fun because she is so passionate about it and she loves Hunger Games so much, even just finding subtle nods back to the movie. She would say, "I wanna do a ladybug look." Thom Browne did that amazing ladybug dress, I thought, "That's so cool, but it's not really her personal aesthetic." So it’s finding ways to keep it still true to her personal style while maintaining the nods to the film.

The way you seem to understand Mckenna feels something similar to the connection between Katniss and Cinna in The Hunger Games. When pulling looks for her, what comes into play? How do you make her come through and not be lost in the lore of the stories or the dress?

Mckenna had mentioned that she maybe wanted to do a red or a dark pink feather look because in the books [Maysilee] gets attacked by the red birds which are like flamingos. I'm pulling in all these red feather dresses and on the runway, this one dress looked amazing. Mckenna said, “That's perfect for the flamingo reference.”.

But we put it on her and it was so big, and she's so petite so she was just getting swarmed. I noted, “Let"s not force it.” The goal was for her to feel comfortable in the look rather than just getting each reference.

Recent findings suggest that the public has been really excited about these looks. Are you thinking about the response to the looks when you’re putting them together?

There's been some conversations in a fitting, like, "Oh, the Hunger Games fans are gonna get this." They're gonna see the inspiration, they're gonna understand it.

But I wouldn't say we're choosing a look because ‘Oh, this is gonna go viral to the Hunger Games community.’ Mckenna is a super fan herself so if she's getting excited about the look, everyone else that's a fan of the franchise is gonna get excited about the look.

Mckenna Grace in Betsey Johnson.

Do you feel any pressure to top the last outfit after each premiere?

Recent findings suggest that yes. I think it was Paris because that wedding dress did get so much press. In that fitting, it felt like, "We gotta keep our game up high." It's been really fun for my team and market assistants because a lot of the girls that work with me are huge fans of the movie. They're not even seeing it as work. They're like, "Oh my God, this is so exciting. Look at this. This looks like this from the movie.".

What was the inspiration to do method dressing for this press run? What do you think is the value?

Recent findings suggest that mckenna knew back in April, she said, "I wanna do method for this." I personally did not read the books. I'm a visual person, so I've seen all the movies. Lionsgate was able to let me go with the cast when they first saw the movie because my agent was like, "Molly needs to go to the movie to get inspired before this press tour. She can't do a method dressing press tour without seeing the movie.".

Even as the tour was going on, Mckenna kept sending me newly introduced references and quotes from the book and stuff like that.

Sources indicate that what made you take it to the next level? From paying homage to not only characters, but the actual actors from the films like Jennifer Lawrence at the 2011 Oscars to even dressing like set pieces from the film.

That was all Mckenna's vision. On her first mood board, she had a lot of Jennifer Lawrence's red carpet moments because she's such a huge fan of Katniss and Jennifer Lawrence.

In a recent development, with the Rue reference, Mckenna thought that color was just very Hunger Games. It wasn't until she put the dress on, her mom said, "Wait, this is Rue's dress." So that was just fate. I would love to take credit for that.

Why do you think that this styling has generated so much attention?

I think it’s when you do method dressing for such a significant franchise and you really are passionate about it. The thing is that Mckenna is so excited and passionate about this movie. She has noted, “I didn't think that I would love doing fittings so much. I used to hate doing fittings.”.

Mckenna Grace in Elisabetta Franchi.

Because every look is so intentionally tied back to Hunger Games and she's such a massive fan, it's literally like playing dress up with her. I think the fans see it, she's so relatable because she's a fan that all these fans think, "Wow, like, she's a fan and she got to do this." She’s the fangirl living out her dream, and the fans are excited for her that she finally gets to do this.

What do you think are the best kinds of projects to implement method dressing with/works best with? What does it work best with?

Industry observers note that I think the major movies that already have a fan base, like Barbie or Wednesday, Being able to pull inspiration from existing books or films makes it so much easier for a stylist rather than a movie that no one's seen before. There's no curiosity or momentum about it because you're starting from scratch, whereas Hunger Games, Barbie, Wednesday, there's already a level of expectation.

Sources indicate that the looks for this press run have been a mix of archival, new, and custom pieces. How do you make that choice? How important is it for you to create an archive for Mckenna?

In a recent development, it kind of is a mix of what we’re able to source. Mckenna really wanted to pay homage to Joanna's character with that scene where she's like, "My stylist is always putting me in trees." She's like, "I wanna do a tree reference." And I'm like, "How in the world am I gonna find a fashion reference that's a tree that's not a costume?".

Recent findings suggest that I love the challenge of sourcing the market, and so do the girls on my team. I think it was 2011 Phoebe Philo where Celine did some tree references in the collection. But just because we find it online doesn't mean that we can get it. So then it's reaching out to every vintage dealer, every rental house, asking, "Do you guys have anything like this?" And they might have it, but they're like, "It's already gone, someone has it." I ended up actually finding the Celine tree dress on the RealReal, and I bought it. I love RealReal.

According to recent reports, what is your approach to dressing different clients? For instance, you mentioned Sadie Sink earlier, can you walk me through how that process differs from Mckenna?

According to recent reports, it's very different between each girl. I let them set the pace. If they wanna be involved, great. If they just wanna show up to the fitting and not even know what's gonna be there, I try to accommodate whatever direction they wanna go. I have one client that literally last week has sent me over 200 references of dresses that she wants, and another girl that's like, “I really don't care. Whatever you tell me to wear, I'll wear it.”.

Every girl is different, and what makes my job so interesting is that it's not the same. Everyone has very different styles. I think the most notable part of a job as a stylist is to keep their style true to them and not just force my style onto them. Mckenna's way more girly, Sadie is a little bit more casual, it’s just taking their style and elevating it a little bit.

Will you do any looks inspired by Mckenna’s character Maysilee? The looks have been mostly referential to things and people from past stories. Are there influences of Maysilee in the looks that fans haven't been able to pick up on because the film wasn’t out yet?

According to recent reports, in a couple days, she’ll be in Miami for press, and she's wearing a very Maysilee inspired, purple Miu Miu dress that has a white collar. When she wears it, everyone's gonna be like, "Oh, that's Maysilee." She really wanted to have flowers and necklaces because Maysilee is really into jewelry, so it’s very light and flowery.

Can you break down the outfit for the New York City premiere?

We are doing the Mockingjay dress, the one with the wings, and that was another thing that I was very stumped on. I'm like, "What designer's gonna make these wings?" I had this woman in LA who does wings, she's done Halloween costumes and music videos.

Mckenna Grace in Pamella Roland.

In a recent development, in the first fitting, I pulled this navy Pamella Roland gown. The fabric is really, really cool. It's like a shimmery kind of organza. I thought, "That's the right color,” but I wanted it to be strapless. I went back to Pamella Roland and they were like, "We can make it in strapless." Mckenna was very keen on having some sort of embellishment to replicate Katniss because she had screen printing on the gown and it kind of looks like wings in a way.

Sources indicate that pamella then drew all these CADs with diamond wings on it, and then we got the wings made. We did the final fitting and I almost started to cry. Her mom's taking videos and it's epic. It's so exciting because the fans were doing polls on what she's gonna wear to the premiere.

It's full circle, we started with the wedding dress, Mckenna did the fire gown, and then we ended with the Mockingjay dress.

What was the hardest look to pull together?

Mckenna Grace in custom Cong Tri.

I think design-wise, it was the fire gown.

Getting the fire printed on the fabric was really hard. I had a while back done a custom Cong Tri gown for Cami Mendes for the Masters of the Universe tour. It was like a gold beaded gown, and I remember I really liked the fabrics that they used for it.

In a recent development, so when I was thinking of who could do this fire gown, I reached out to them first, and I'm like, "Can you guys do something that looks like a fire? Like, she's literally on fire." And they're like, "No. We don't think we can." And again, they were like, "Give us some time." They came back and said, "We did all these testing on the fabric." I'm like, "Yeah, you did it. You did it.".

What's really funny is we were at a fitting at Mckenna's house with the fire gown in a garment bag, and one of her friends stopped by. It was just a tip of the dress showing and her friend stated, "Oh my God, you got a fire gown." Then I thought, "Okay, people are gonna get it.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Among the many, many side activities you can do in GTA 6, there's powerwashing.
  • According to recent reports, A question had been asked and an answer was required.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Among the many, many side activities you can do in GTA 6, there's powerwashing. Relatively early on, as part of Chapter 1's Down to Earth mission, Jason whips out his nozzle and blasts Brian's boat to a gleaming sheen. Disappointingly for powerwashing fans, though, it's a bit of a one-and-done gag, never to return. But powerwashing is powerwashing, and we immediately wondered what the experts made of it all. Had Rockstar, with its legendary attention to detail, accurately captured the intricacies of powerwashing in those leisurely moments of carefree squirting?

According to recent reports, A question had been asked and an answer was required. So who better to cast judgement on the authenticity of Jason's sway-and-spraying than FuturLab, the studio behind the delightfully zen PowerWash Simulator series? Thus, in a moment of whimsy, I asked if it might like to 'review' GTA 6's hosiest activity. At best, I was hoping for a cheeky little statement; I certainly wasn't expecting a major chunk of the PowerWash Simulator 2 team to join in the fun. "Fair to say," the intermediary PR noted, "the Futurlab team was excited about this one!".

Recent findings suggest that so what's the verdict? Let us turn to the pros. "They've got the sounds and satisfaction of clearly a nice shiny flat surface just right," PowerWash Simulator 2 lead game designer Nick McCarthy opined, "but where's the ding!? 0/10, needs 200 percent more layers of muck and 20 percent more parkour." And quickly a trend emerged. "Great visuals, satisfying feel, but lacks the crucial ding and went by too quickly to listen to a podcast," senior programmer Will Dyball wrote. Then still more sadness for the lack of PowerWash Simulator's most motivating sound: "Didn't hear a ding," associate publishing producer Jess Crosby wrote. "Must have missed a bit.".

A few team members also spotted some powerwashing faux pas. "No soap?" wrote 3D artist Eilidh Norris. "Rookie mistake, Jason." Programmer Jordan Lewis also reckoned Jason was making things unnecessarily hard for himself: "[He'd] have had an easier time had he taken the time to upgrade his washer and purchased some more nozzles," they wrote. "PS. Soap would have gotten that off in a flash." Others had safety concerns: "I find Jason's lack of protective overalls disturbing," mentioned 3D artist Rory Peace, and data principal Russell Young agreed. "Clean speedboat, ruined clothes. Don't want to bring them 'Down to Earth', but we need to talk about PPE." People advisor Sarah Robshaw, meanwhile, spotted a more heinous omission: "Where's the cats????".

Recent findings suggest that elsewhere, game designer Sam Jenkins was delighted by the powerwashing representation. "I'm so glad that the Art of Powerwashing is being taken more seriously in mainstream games!" they wrote. "However, I think the dirt on the boat is too scarce for that satisfying cleaning contrast to come through.".

Jenkins even had some expert suggestions to make Jason's little squirt-out more rewarding: "Maybe the boat should have been left in a flooded warehouse for 30 years to coat it in grime?" they continued. "Or even have a crushed fruit festival come through town to get some nice major colourful blobs all over the boat. Ooh! And we could even have the boat be the home of various squids to get some difficult-to-clean Ink streaked down it too!" Truly the words of someone who takes their powerwashing seriously!

Junior build engineer Owen Layton, programmer Jordan Lewis, and lead designer Nick McCarthy also provided 'reviews' in pictoral form, but technical complications mean they'll just have to exist in your imagination. Senior narrative designer Mark Ginbey, though, expressed admiration for all the in-world encouragement players are given. "Some excellent motivational text updates from Cal, like 'Mmhmm, half way there...' to indicate 50 percent completion," they wrote. "But Jason needs to concentrate on the work in hand. A quality powerwasher never talks on the job.".

Recent findings suggest that senior game designer António Salreta had praise for GTA 6, with one exception: "It's an amazing game with so many fun systems - but. Needs. More. Nozzles." And how's this for a ringing endorsement from senior QA tester Paul Comse? "I love coming home after a hard day of work powerwashing in PowerWash Sim and unwinding by powerwashing some more in GTA," they wrote. But if we're scoring Jason's efforts? "7.8/10, too much water.".

Recent findings suggest that so there you go! The experts have spoken, and I'd call it a success for Rockstar's inaugural attempt at powerwashing, despite a handful of 'must try harders'. An unexpectedly generous response indeed! And if you're curious how FuturLab does it, look no further than last year's PowerWash Simulator 2. And for help with powerwashing in GTA 6, we've got a guide.

Industry observers note that A novel solution for connecting to the internet on the go, the TP-Link Roam 7 travel router is now down to $83.49 from $119.99 for Black Friday, marking its lowest price to date. This isn't a full-size home router but, as the name suggests, a compact travel companion that measures roughly the size of a paperback book, with foldable antennas that let it slip easily into a bag.

More about convenience than chasing top speeds, you can use the Roam 7 as a standard router, connect it to public wifi to create a private network, or share your phone's internet through USB tethering. It also supports Ethernet input and USB modems, along with range extender and wireless client modes. That flexibility is particularly useful when you’re juggling a laptop, phone, and maybe a tablet and would prefer not to sign each one into a shaky network separately. Setup is straightforward through the TP-Link Tether app: scan a QR code, choose your connection type, and you’re online in a few minutes.

Once it’s running, the hardware covers the basics, with a 2.5 Gbps port for a wired connection like a hotel’s Ethernet jack, a 1 Gbps port for a wired device, and a USB 3.0 port for a storage drive or phone tethering. And since it draws power over USB-C (5V/3A), a basic power bank can keep it going through a long layover or a camping trip. As handy as it is on the road, though, it’s not meant to replace a full-size home router—even with its 5 GHz band and Wi-Fi 7 support—which will generally offer better coverage and more consistent speeds. Real-world performance also depends heavily on your connection and setup. USB tethering, for example, can feel slower than using your phone directly. It also leaves out features like automatic band steering, so you may end up managing networks yourself. Still, if you travel often or need a portable network hub for multiple devices, you’ll find it holds up pretty well.

However, the various bits from those original Meet the Parents movies have stuck with me. So, I was thrilled to see so many A+ references to them in Focker In-Law. However, there was one callback in this project on the 2026 movie schedule that was very extreme.

As was to be expected when Ariana Grande joined Focker In-Law as the newest potential in-law, hijinks and lie detector tests were going to happen. Plus, with Ben Stiller’s Greg now in the position Robert De Niro’s Jack was in during the first movie, the script was flipped, which provided a fun foundation to return to some very funny gags.

First of all, I thought the way they brought the lie detector back into this movie was delightful. Watching Olivia be tested was really funny, and knowing that Greg had to go through a much tougher version of that in Meet the Parents made the whole situation even better.

Sources indicate that getting into a specific Easter egg, I wasn’t expecting the Gaylord callbacks in this movie at all. As you might remember, Greg Focker’s legal name is Gaylord Focker. And in Focker In-Law, that comes up because his daughter, Samantha (Beanie Feldstein), will use it every now and again. I loved how casual the reference was, and I couldn't help but chuckle at the "if you know, you know" nature of this whole ongoing joke.

According to recent reports, of course, there were many other A+ Easter eggs and jokes that called back to the earlier movies – like everything having to do with the Circle of Trust and Owen Wilson’s character, Kevin. However, the one I really can’t get over has to do with Jinx the cat.

Sources indicate that I expected some wild things to happen in Focker In-Law. To this day, I remember the shock I felt over the absolutely crazy situations that happened in Meet the Parents and Meet the Fockers (which you can stream with a Peacock subscription). However, I did not expect Jinx the cat to be taxidermied. I did not expect Jack’s dog, Lazarus, to have beef with the late cat. And I certainly did not expect the German shepherd to eat the taxidermied Jinx in the movie.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Recent findings suggest that really, any moment involving the iconic cat made me crack up. I couldn’t get over the fact that they paid homage to him by having him taxidermied.

However, it was when Jinx got involved in a battle between Greg and Lazarus that I couldn’t keep it together. In an effort to get the dog off his back, Greg grabbed the cat and threw it. The dog went after it and ripped it to shreds.

Industry observers note that my jaw was legitimately on the floor when this happened, and I was laughing so hard I was crying. Honestly, I couldn’t believe they went there with Jinxie. I mean, that cat was Jack's pride and joy, and now he's been ripped to shreds. However, it added to the glorious absurdity of this film.

Now, if you’d like to see this wild moment for yourself, you can catch Focker In-Law in theaters now.

Nicole Scherzinger and fiancé Thom Evans have ended their relationship after seven years together.

Industry observers note that “It is with a heavy heart that I share that Nicole and I are no longer together,” Evans, 41, wrote via his Instagram Story on Friday, November 27. “After seven years of love, commitment and believing in a future together, this is an incredibly difficult time.”.

According to recent reports, he continued: “Whilst this is not the outcome I had ever hoped for, I respect Nicole’s decision and genuinely wish her every happiness in the next chapter of her life. Thom x.”.

Scherzinger, 48, for her part, has yet to publicly address the breakup.

Recent findings suggest that the former couple met in 2019 on the set of The X Factor: Celebrity. They began dating later that year but didn’t go public with their romance until a Golden Globe Awards afterparty red carpet in 2020.

Industry observers note that “It wasn’t even in my thought process to try it on with Nicole because it would have been unprofessional, and she’s so lovely and stunning in every possible way,” Evans told The Sun in 2021. “I was just like, ‘She’s out of my league.'”.

Recent findings suggest that he added: “It was only after [my band Try Star] sang an awkward performance of ‘Swing Low, Sweet Chariot’ and she kindly saved us in the show that we, as a band, went up to her dressing room to thank her. That was the first time I met her, and I’ve never looked back.”.

Three years later, the former rugby player popped the question. Scherzinger teased that the pair were planning on having a wedding in her native Hawaii with a reception in Europe.

GTA 6 causes surge in UK physical game sales, despite there being no disc in the box

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 has had a huge effect on physical game sales in the UK, despite not actually containing a disc in the box.
  • NielsenIQ data shows that GTA 6 drove boxed software sales up an enormous 409 percent for the launch period ending 21st November, compared to the previous week, resulting in the biggest week for UK physical game sales since Christmas 2018.
  • GTA 6 alone accounted for £32m of the total £43m boxed software sales, apparently - around 74 percent, with 88 percent of its sales generated on day-one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has had a huge effect on physical game sales in the UK, despite not actually containing a disc in the box.

NielsenIQ data shows that GTA 6 drove boxed software sales up an enormous 409 percent for the launch period ending 21st November, compared to the previous week, resulting in the biggest week for UK physical game sales since Christmas 2018.

GTA 6 alone accounted for £32m of the total £43m boxed software sales, apparently - around 74 percent, with 88 percent of its sales generated on day-one. But it's not a champion or record-breaker in this regard. In fact, GTA 6 places 17th in the all-time table of first-week boxed revenue, which is refreshingly humbling given the money-making records it's been breaking elsewhere. This is to do with the overwhelming shift towards buying games digitally, of course.

Nevertheless, Rockstar is well represented in the all-time list (which stretches back to 1995), because it's none other than GTA 5 that sits at the top, and GTA 4 at 11th.

But the GTA 6 effect is that of a rising tide, with console hardware sales rising 38 percent, to their highest level since 2025. Specifically, PS5 sales rose 46 percent and Xbox Series sales jumped a considerable 75 percent. And it's been a similar result in the US, where PS5 and Xbox Series sales have more than doubled.

Gaming accessory sales also got a boost, with PS5 controller sales up 355 percent, gaming headset sales up 94 percent, and - more nichely - gaming chair sales up 32 percent, which is apparently in line with the 40 percent increase they experienced around GTA 5.

It has been revealed that "While the physical games market looks very different today compared with previous blockbuster releases, GTA 6 has still made a huge impact," mentioned NielsenIQ's Dorian Bloch. "Back in 2008, boxed software accounted for half of all games retail revenue for the combined sectors of software, hardware, and gaming accessories, compared with 15 percent so far in 2026. This is a reflection of the market increasingly shifting towards digital downloads.".

According to recent reports, it's against this backdrop, of course, that Sony made its hugely controversial decision to wind down production of PlayStation game discs starting January 2028. This has led to boycotts and backlash and much angry sentiment towards the manufacturer, but Grand Theft Auto 6's enormous digital success is likely to be a hard example to ignore.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that “Cancer does change you,” Kate Middleton states, emotion clear in her voice. “It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.” These words come not at as an Instagram post or at a public event. Instead, they're the voice-over in a previously unannounced documentary about the Princess of Wales and her life since she disclosed a diagnosis of cancer in 2024.

According to Kensington Palace, which announced the film on Saturday, Heal is “a deeply personal newly introduced documentary from The Princess of Wales, exploring life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.” It will air on the BBC in the UK on November 29, and in the US on NBCUniversal on November 30.

Sources indicate that heal follows Kate Middleton during her participation in one of the United Kingdom’s most demanding endurance events: The National Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed this summer. In less than 24 hours, the princess climbed the three highest mountains in Scotland, England, and Wales: Ben Nevis (4,413 feet), Scafell Pike (3,209 feet), and Yr Wyddfa–Snowdon (3,559 feet). The undertaking wasn't just a personal effort, as it was also in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, an organization that supports people living with cancer before, during, and after the disease.

The documentary will also support that organization, Kensington Palace notes, saying “All funds received through the documentary's distribution have been directed to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity to help people living with and beyond cancer.” The Royal Marsden Hospital, at which Middleton received treatment, is also referenced in the film, as Middleton's brother, James, asks her “Isn’t it when you leave the Royal Marsden, you ring the bell?”.

It has been revealed that but while many patients participate in the bell-ringing ritual at the conclusion of treatment, Middleton says she missed out on that moment. “Yeah, but I didn’t ring the bell,” she replies. “So maybe this is your ringing of the bell,” James responded, suggesting her Three Peaks experience was that symbolic peal.

While Prince William is no stranger to documentary work, nor are Prince Harry and wife Meghan Markle, this is Kate Middleton's first venture into the format. Perhaps to ease her into the project, Heal's Director of Photography is a face quite familiar to the Princess: Will Warr, the filmmaker behind her video announcement marking the end of her chemotherapy treatments.

“Through this documentary, The Princess hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer and transform access to holistic cancer care which supports wellbeing, resilience and quality of life during and after diagnosis,” Kensington Palace indicates of Heal, a message underscored by Middleton's words in the trailer. “You know, healing is a journey. How to reconnect with the things you once knew and how to find a sense of hope and joy alongside uncertainty.”.

“It’s clear we're not meant to face life’s challenges alone,” the princess says as the trailer concludes. “Things can renew and grow. Often it is through pain that we realize that there is a greater beauty that lies beyond that.".

If you're looking for a portable Bluetooth speaker, for instance, you don't want to buy something with poor sound quality, or that doesn't easily connect to your devices, or that breaks unexpectedly.

It has been revealed that you don't need to worry about any of that with the JBL Go 4. This is a solid portable speaker that just so happens to have an MSRP of $49.95. It's so good, I named it Lifehacker's best gift under $50, as its price, excellent sound quality, and feature set make it a great option for most anyone on your list. It's an even better buy during Black Friday, too: Right now, you can pick up the JBL Go 4 for as low as $31.95, 36% off the original retail price.

JBL's Go 4 is a small speaker, but it gets surprisingly loud—especially for a speaker at this price point. Like other JBL speakers, it places a particular emphasis on bass. This is a tiny speaker, so don't expect a subwoofer on the go, but not only will it let you hear the bass in your music, it is noticeably punchy. JBL advertises seven hours of playtime on a single charge here, which is often plenty for taking the speaker out and about for the day. You can net an additional two hours of if you engage "Playtime Boost." JBL doesn't specify how this works, but it likely cuts some of the frequencies here to save on battery life. And, since it's 1P67-rated against dust and water, it's a great choice for outdoor use.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps my favorite thing about the JBL Go 4 is that it supports Auracast. That means you can easily connect to any other Auracast-compatible JBL speaker using the Auracast button on each device. I've used this before at parties and gatherings for an impromptu multi-speaker setup. Since JBL is so popular, it's not impractical to assume one or two other people at the function might have a similar speaker you can connect to, or if you know friends or family members have JBL speakers of their own, you can coordinate these setups ahead of time.

This discount is only available on specific colors of the Go 4, at least on Amazon: Black, White, Blue, Purple, Red, and "Squad." Black and Orange, Pink, and Sand are all still $49.95. Again, the JBL Go 4 is absolutely worth the $50 MSRP, but unless you're married to one of those three colors, it's even better at a discount.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Nioh and Ninja Gaiden studio is using AI for QA, but argues "that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands"

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (386 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Team Ninja (Nioh, Ninja Gaiden) is the latest game development studio to implement AI into some of its workflow, but producer Kohei Shibata still believes that fun games need to be "crafted by human hands.".
  • The producer best known for the tough-as-nails Nioh trilogy and Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty spoke about the controversial tech during South Korea's GCON 2026, in an interview with INVEN Global.
  • It has been revealed that he went on to argue that if AI can "shorten task times," then developers can spend more hours "elevating the game's overall quality" in other ways.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Team Ninja (Nioh, Ninja Gaiden) is the latest game development studio to implement AI into some of its workflow, but producer Kohei Shibata still believes that fun games need to be "crafted by human hands.".

The producer best known for the tough-as-nails Nioh trilogy and Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty spoke about the controversial tech during South Korea's GCON 2026, in an interview with INVEN Global. "Right now, we utilize AI in QA and various verification tasks to streamline certain workflows," Shibata explained.

It has been revealed that he went on to argue that if AI can "shorten task times," then developers can spend more hours "elevating the game's overall quality" in other ways. "In that sense, using AI is beneficial." Team Ninja isn't fully on board with enforcing the tech elsewhere, though: "Since it's still a upcoming technology, we are continuously evaluating the most appropriate ways to implement it. I imagine other game companies are facing similar questions." (Good spot, Kotaku.).

It has been revealed that "What matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands. Repetitive, simple tasks that anyone must perform can be streamlined using technology. But ultimately, deciding how to craft the game and what makes it enjoyable must be done by humans. Using AI itself should never become the goal. I believe the principle that humans must think for themselves and finish the game will remain unchanged in the future," Shibata continued.

Generative AI's use in game development is still a hotly debated topic among both players and the people making games, but it's been prevalent nonetheless. A recent report estimated that around 40 percent of game developers were using AI in some fashion, even if lots of them also agreed the tech was harmful. Bigger publishers like Ubisoft and Epic Games are more aggressively pursuing an AI-first future, too.

In a recent development, team Ninja seems to be settling into a middle ground, at least, according to Shibata's statement. Speaking on the studio's approach to difficult games, he mentioned that a player's failure should never be the game's fault. Dying in a game like Ninja Gaiden or Nioh should always be the result of human error, otherwise death "causes frustration." Finding that perfect, often bloody sweet spot is something only humans can do.

Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6Rockstar GamesUnion.

According to recent reports, rockstar Games will not be forced to formally recognize a union at the Grand Theft Auto 6 studio after its developers based in the UK voted overwhelmingly against the initiative. The weeks-long voting process played out as Rockstar launched the open-world hit to over 30 million sales in its first day.

Recent findings suggest that voting began on November 12 and concluded today on November 26. Workers at Rockstar Games voted 75 percent against the recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union. The initiate would have formalized collective bargaining efforts around things like overtime, bonuses, layoffs, and AI. Developers in favor of unionizing can still work with the IGWB, but there will be no regular meetings with management to hash out fresh policies.

Sources indicate that “We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6,” Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe remarked in a statement shared with Kotaku. “This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together.â.

The IWGB Game Workers Union pushing the vote released the following statement:.

According to recent reports, for anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society – this isnât a sign to retreat, itâs a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. Weâre ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

In a recent development, whilst we havenât emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.

Industry observers note that A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But itâs one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. Weâll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.

The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.

Sources indicate that the vote comes roughly a year after Rockstar fired dozens of developers it accused of gross misconduct and breaking confidentiality rules around the development of GTA 6. The fired workers accused the studio of union busting, which it has denied, and a legal fight has been ongoing over the last 12 months at a labor tribunal. A final judgement in that case is still pending. As recently as this month, members of both sides of the dispute were testifying on the record for the case.
