📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developer CD Projekt Red has rolled out a fresh patch for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered on all platforms, which squashes dozens of bugs and adds 40 cross-platform mods with "more on the way.".

"Two things are certain in a witcher's life: the Path never sleeps, and the work is never done," the studio wrote in its latest exhaustive list of patch notes for the decade-old game.

Patch 5.02's handiest changes come from those aforementioned bug fixes, many of which once caused the game to crash entirely or simply not work as intended. One such bug caused "time to go backwards indefinitely." Another turned Geralt bald. Opening the game with outdated mods could also result in a crash on PC. All of those, plus plenty more, have been fixed.

When The Witcher 3 Remastered first dropped, many players also took problem with the game's updated and sometimes "lifeless" lighting. Previous CDPR patches already targeted the lighting changes in question, but this newest patch continues to fix "various lighting issues across multiple locations and cutscenes.".

The studio specifically names "overly bright or dark areas" and "inconsistent lighting transitions and flickering.".

It has been revealed that the Witcher 3's free remastered upgrade also gave all console owners access to mod support, though not all pre-existing PC mods were available to download for console folks. This patch is expanding the selection somewhat with 40 upcoming cross-platform mods, including glowy eyes for Geralt and a new monster hunt - and on social media, the studio promised "more on the way.".

CD Projekt Red is still hard at work on two big upcoming sequels, The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2. Speaking on the former in a recent earnings call, joint-CEO Michal Nowakowski said we can expect a similar leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 as we've just seen from GTA 5 to GTA 6.

According to recent reports, it's official: After more than five years together and nearly a year of engagement, Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando have tied the knot. The couple were married in the desert hot spot of Palm Springs, California on Saturday, November 21, an outdoor ceremony held at Frank Sinatra’s former mansion, with Wayne Coyne, frontman of The Flaming Lips and a Cyrus collaborator, officiating.

The 33-year-old singer and the 28-year-old musician—Morando is the drummer for the band Liily—had kept their prepares a secret until Friday, when TMZ broke the news. Confirmation of the impending celebration emerged that same evening, during the dinner that capped off the rehearsal, when Miley’s half-sister, Lily-Rose Purcell, posted a photo on her Instagram Stories of a menu featuring the couple’s initials. This is Cyrus’s second marriage, following her alliance with actor Liam Hemsworth from 2018 to 2019.

Sinatra’s former home in Palm Springs, where the wedding took place.

According to images published in outlets including People, the ceremony venue was decorated with white flowers and large candles, with Sinatra’s pool in the background. Miley Cyrus wore a long-sleeved white satin dress with a plunging back and no veil, while the groom opted for a classic black tuxedo with a bow tie.

Among the guests were the bride’s mother, Tish Cyrus, accompanied by her husband, actor Dominic Purcell, and Miley's sister, Noah Cyrus. Also in attendance was the singer’s father, Billy Ray Cyrus, along with his rumored fiancée, British actress Elizabeth Hurley, and her son, Damian.

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando on February 01, 2026.

Industry observers note that as the bride has recounted in past interviews, her relationship with her now-husband began in 2021 following a blind date organized by mutual friends. That same year, they went public by attending the singer’s Latest Year’s Eve TV special in Miami together. Their engagement came to light in December 2025, when, during another of those joint appearances, Miley Cyrus posed on the red carpet wearing a diamond ring that turned out to be her engagement ring.

One of the most emotional moments of the ceremony took place just before the couple exchanged their vows, when—according to multiple outlets— Dolly Parton’s “Love Is Like a Butterfly” began to play. The nod follows a similar one Miley made last month, when she broke down in tears over Parton's death during a performance at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles.

Recent findings suggest that “Me and Dolly, we are eternal. Nothing in this life could ever tear us apart, and I’m gonna see her again,” Cyrus told the stadium crowd in October, per The Hollywood Reporter. “And I can’t fucking wait because I miss her,” Cyrus tearfully continued. “Some of the greatest music that we have today was written, produced, performed by my Aunt Dolly.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I write a lot about e-readers and e-ink tablets for Lifehacker, and one problem I'm constantly grappling with is how to write informatively about a bunch of devices that can be quite different in some details, like build or native firmware, and pretty much identical in others, given that literally all e-ink devices use display technology produced by the same Chinese company. (It's called E-Ink.) The best way to do this is to include more video in my articles, but I've lacked a good way to film hands-free so I can easily demonstrate a device's look and feel—until recently.

I recently got an offer to try out a magnetic neck mount from Telesin, a low-cost option to turn my iPhone into a wearable so I can keep my hands free while filming. It's a pretty basic concept, but well-executed: The band that goes around your neck is made of rubber with a firm but flexible core, so you can easily position it to be longer or shorter or at an angle, and the phone mount is on an extending arm with three joints to give you additional options.

I haven't had a chance to film anything for public consumption quite yet, but my testing has already given me some great ideas for how I can use it to show off, say, what it's really like to use a micro-reader in comparison to a full-sized Kindle, as I'll be able to wear it to give a more accurate user's point of view. And right now is a good time to pick one of them up, as many of Telesin's phone and camera accessories (including similar models built to handle an action camera like a GoPro) are discounted for Black Friday; the one I tested is down to $17, or 15% off.

This won't be the right device for every filming scenario. Though MagSafe holds my iPhone fairly securely, I found that I would accidentally detach it every time I tried to adjust the shooting angle—once even leading me to drop it. That's potentially bad news, as using it may require you to take the phone out of its case if it isn't MagSafe-compatible. (Mine isn't.) But if you're just looking for an inexpensive way to shoot hands-free video in a controlled environment, it could be exactly what you need.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that EA is ditching seasonal updates and shaving some of the live service fluff off Skate (for some reason stylised as skate.) going forward.
  • Industry observers note that "EA and Full Circle are committed to keep driving skate.
  • Skate's fifth and final season is coming to an end on 1st December, with Full Circle embracing a different model from there on out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that EA is ditching seasonal updates and shaving some of the live service fluff off Skate (for some reason stylised as skate.) going forward. Normally, such news would be cause for concern. Here, the publisher assured players the transition will lead to more regular updates since devs can now push out latest features without waiting for the next season to roll around.

Industry observers note that "EA and Full Circle are committed to keep driving skate. forward. Just as a reminder, we're still very much in Early Access," the studio wrote in a newly introduced blog post. "The game is still a work in progress, and we're using this valuable time to experiment, iterate, and figure out what works best for the long-term health of the game - especially when it comes to social features and progression. Ultimately, we want to build skate. in a way that lets us roll out fresh content much faster, even if it's not totally finished yet.".

Skate's fifth and final season is coming to an end on 1st December, with Full Circle embracing a different model from there on out. "We are transitioning away from the traditional seasonal cadence in favor of regular, agile content updates," it explained.

It has been revealed that full Circle is also throwing out the skating sim's version of a seasonal battle pass (horribly named skate.Pass) by the end of the year, and will rethink how the game's progression system works: "We've remarked it many times: we have a long-term future vision for skate, and this is a key part of it. Update 0.33.1 will be our very first update in this post-season era.".

Sources indicate that the move away from rigid seasonal updates "gives the development team the freedom to launch features earlier in their lifecycle," the blog post continued. "This means we can deploy work-in-progress mechanics and gather your direct feedback to continuously shape and build upon San Vansterdam. We've started this with in-game testing of features such as Spot Battles, Block Parties, and Prox Chat before rolling it out officially, and we’re going to continue with this process.".

According to recent reports, full Circle's live service rejig also means the in-game currency Tix is being retired, and some maps will no longer be locked behind paywalls. Skate still has real-money microtransactions and a cosmetics store, though it's nice to see some of the more aggressive live service bits being plucked out.

Ugh. It’s my least-favorite time of year: Black Friday season. I hate this overwhelming capitalist-ass shopping holiday for many reasons, but one of my more petty pet peeves is the big push for the blandest, most cringey “gamer”-themed gifts ever at mainstream shopping destinations. I’m talking like, this “Smells like video game rage” candle, neon lights and blankets that say stuff like, “Can’t hear you, I’m gaming,” or the classic “I paused my game to be here” T-shirt. Crap that really leans into the awful “gamer” stereotype and that, for many of us, is embarrassing to receive from a relative who knows, like, one fact about us, which is that we are into video games.

If you’ve arrived at this article and have been guilty of giving such gifts before, please absolve yourself. The internet does not make this easy. Gaming gift guides are full of this junk, and if you’re not into games yourself, finding decent stuff for someone who likes them can be really annoying and challenging, especially on a budget. Most gamers probably have a lot of the tech and games they want already, and knowing what people have and what they might like can be extremely challenging if you don’t have an easy way to look at their Steam libraries.

According to recent reports, so I’m here to give you a hand with 12 ideas for stocking stuffer gifts (read: will reasonably fit in a normal-sized Christmas stocking) under $30 that will probably be relevant to folks who like playing video games on the regular. These are all things that most people will be at least mildly pleased to receive and will probably use as long as you put in the bare minimum amount of thought to make sure you’re not getting Switch accessories for someone who doesn’t have a Switch or something.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One person who has been the talk of the town in the world of celebrity fashion is Julianne Hough. As Dancing with the Stars aired its 35th season on the 2026 TV schedule, she made some very bold outfit choices, and in response, fans did not hold back their opinions on them. Now, her stylist has spoken out about the critical discourse regarding the co-host’s DWTS ensembles.

According to recent reports, I’ll be the first to admit that when Julianne Hough walked into the ballroom for a given episode of DWTS, I was often shocked by her outfits. They were bold, sometimes avant-garde and always fun to see. According to her stylist, Brad Goreski, they were trying going for fits that were “super elevated and strong” as well as “super extravagant and wild and playful and colorful and sparkly.” I think they achieved that goal, as you can see in the photos of Hough and her co-host Alfonso Ribeiro below:.

Image credit: Disney/Eric McCandless.

Image credit: Disney/Christopher Willard.

The co-host’s fashion choices throughout the season (which you can see with a Disney+ subscription) led to quite a bit of criticism from fans. One person posted one of Hough’s sheer outfits on Instagram and wrote over it, “Respectfully, who is Julianne’s stylist and why do they need to be fired?” Meanwhile, someone on X stated they thought the people dressing Hough were “playing a cruel joke” on her. These kinds of comments happened week after week.

When Goreski and Hough spoke to Glamour about her style this season, they addressed the backlash that came with it too. The dancer’s stylist noted he has “an awareness” of it. He also explained:.

And I love it. Any conversation, good or bad, around fashion is great. I think people weighing in—they like the hair but not the dress; they thought it was a bad outfit; they think she should fire me—is totally fine, because we’re really excited by what we’re doing, and we put a lot of thought and energy into it. I think Jules ultimately brings the looks to life, and I’m glad that there’s another part of the show that people talk about. Not every person’s going to love every look. I know that from being a stylist for 15 years. And that’s okay.

Well, that’s certainly a good mentality to have about all this. Along with that, Hough noted that evolving her style came with risk too. Millions of people watch DWTS, and as her stylist explained, not everyone will like her looks. So, with that being mentioned, the co-host stated that her motto this season was “apathy is the enemy.” She also had this to say about how people react to her fashion choices:.

According to recent reports, the reason things exist and have charge and stay visible [is] people either love it or hate it. They still want to talk about it.

To that point, there were lots of moments on DWTS this year that got people on the internet talking, like liftgate, Jennifer Lawrence trolling Connor Wood, and Ezra Frech making it through his freestyle after his prosthetic fell off. Overall, Season 35 was met with a whole lot of love, but also quite a bit of intense discourse too. And yes, part of that had to do with Julianne Hough's fashion choices.

However, as both the co-host and her stylist said, part of the fun of fashion is getting people talking about it.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Per Automaton, this "early retirement" program is part of an effort to restructure its console business, which refers to non-mobile, non-live-service games under its umbrella.
  • The reason for this change is the shifting environment in game development, namely the growing scope of development and elongated development cycles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marvelous, the studio known for its work on the Story of Seasons series as well as the upcoming Eternal Anima, has announced the introduction of a voluntary redundancy scheme. Through this program, it's aiming to lower its headcount by 65 employees.

Per Automaton, this "early retirement" program is part of an effort to restructure its console business, which refers to non-mobile, non-live-service games under its umbrella.

The reason for this change is the shifting environment in game development, namely the growing scope of development and elongated development cycles. The company cites a need to optimise its workforce and shift towards flexibility, per the introduction of the early retirement program.

In a recent development, marvelous will begin gathering applications, with those choosing to take the company up on the offer set to leave at the end of the financial year in March 2027. These employees will receive a bonus as part of their redundancy package, as well as assistance finding new employment elsewhere if they desire it.

Sources indicate that marvelous emphasised that despite this program, it still sees console game development as one of its core businesses. This comes in the same financial year Marvelous reported a 1,105 percent increase in profit between April 2026 - September 2026, credited to overseas sales of both upcoming indie releases and older console games.

Industry News: Bringing Austen, Wharton, and Steinbeck Into the iPhone Age

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s a balmy late-September day in London, and Dolly Alderton is explaining to a befuddled Emma Frost what “iPhone face” means.
  • “You know [how] you look at some faces, like Rosamund Pike’s face—it looks like it’s never seen an iPhone?
  • “So actors who look like they’re comfortable in a period show, rather than feeling inherently modern,” indicates Frost, as understanding dawns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a balmy late-September day in London, and Dolly Alderton is explaining to a befuddled Emma Frost what “iPhone face” means. Frost has never heard the term; her fellow showrunners Alderton and Zoe Kazan have.

“You know [how] you look at some faces, like Rosamund Pike’s face—it looks like it’s never seen an iPhone? It looks like it’s seen a lute and a loom,” Alderton tells Frost.

“So actors who look like they’re comfortable in a period show, rather than feeling inherently modern,” indicates Frost, as understanding dawns. Alderton and Kazan affirm her: “Yes, yes. Exactly.”.

Now that Frost gets it, she turns back to the group’s Zoom screen. “Sorry, what was the question?”.

Industry observers note that kazan began her career as an actor, while Alderton started out as a dating columnist and Frost was a sculptor and painter. Now all three are overseeing vastly different but comparable Netflix period dramas, each based on a classic work of literature: East of Eden (Kazan’s, which was released October 1), Pride and Prejudice (Alderton’s, out December 3), and The Age of Innocence (Frost’s, coming February 18). They’ve gathered in a London conference room at Netflix headquarters for a roundtable discussion about art, work, the unique experience of adapting a beloved book—and, apparently, iPhone face.

It has been revealed that though this is the first time the trio has met face to face, their conversation flows so easily and naturally that interrupting them with questions sometimes feels impolite. Early on, I note that all three of these novels are, on some level, about unconventional women. Alderton, Frost, and Kazan pause for a moment, considering this Lit 101–level observation.

“That’s true, I think,” agrees Frost.

And then they’re off to more interesting topics.

Vanity Fair: Have you read each other’s books?

Dolly Alderton: No, I haven’t read either of your books.

Alderton: Did you read them at school, or did you read them for fun?

Frost: Pride and Prejudice I read when I was a teenager at school. East of Eden I read first about 15 years ago, I think.

Alderton: So Em already wins the round table.

Frost: And for both of you, was it the thing you most wanted to adapt?

Alderton: I would never have dared to dream to. I was so overwhelmed when I was first approached. I just thought, it’s such a precious IP. It would be way too much, and I wouldn’t be the right person. But then when I was asked to pitch for it, at that point there’s no other answer but yes.

Kazan: First of all, was it the Austen you liked the most?

In a recent development, alderton: Yes. It was the one that I’ve always loved because of Lizzie Bennet. I’ve always been obsessed with Lizzie Bennet. She was my hook. But how about you two? Did you ever dream of adapting these texts?

Frost: I was at a place where I stated, “I want to do anything except period, because I’ve done so much period.” Netflix asked me to do The Age of Innocence, and it was, I think at that moment, the one book that made me just go, “Oh my God, okay, let me go back and revisit it.” Because I know I love it, but you have to know what the reason is [to adapt it again]. And the thing that totally blew me away on a reread was how relevant and resonant it is. It is about the freedom of the individual versus the conformity of the pack. It has so many themes in it that are really resonant with social media, the bullying of the group.

Alderton [turning to Kazan]: Tackling Cathy, how did you begin? What was your way into that?

Recent findings suggest that kazan: I think of adaptation as an advanced form of reading. For me, everything I’ve ever written has come from a feeling of “I have to write this specific thing.” When I was 15 and I read the book for the first time, I felt like it literally grabbed me by the throat and wouldn’t let go. And then I just kept coming back to it. And specifically her character, I felt like I had never read anyone like that before or since.

[to Alderton] The BBC’s Pride and Prejudice—is that the one that you—.

Alderton: No, that wasn’t my Pride and Prejudice.

Alderton: Yeah, the Joe Wright one was the one that I was more familiar with. But I’m so interested in what you were saying about getting to know Cathy. I was kind of nervous about doing press for a book that’s so beloved, and I’m finding it’s actually been really easy so far because I just know the people so well. So much of it has been basically like, putting Mr. Darcy and Elizabeth, all the Bennet family and Bingley through therapy. That psychological interrogation of these very well-known characters has been the thing I’ve just really, really enjoyed.

Recent findings suggest that frost: Have you both had to change points of view from the novel? Do you feel like you’ve had to make a specific choice about who you are foregrounding? I think I know the answer in your case, Zoe.

It has been revealed that kazan: No, I actually don’t. I’m aware that the way that I read a book is different from the way that anyone else reads that book. When I read East of Eden, I feel like I see Steinbeck becoming enthralled by this character, finding her as curious as I do. I think he starts out a real place of judgment and over the course of the book, really moves towards love and understanding.

In a recent development, alderton: I have a similar thing in that for the majority of the book, one of the lead characters is completely unknowable. Not just to Elizabeth, but to the audience as well. So you have to honor that to make it satisfying. That’s kind of frustrating when you’re writing a romantic lead for the first three and a half episodes. None of us, least of all the female protagonist, can see who he is, and we misunderstand him. There is no other option I think than staying with Lizzie.

Recent findings suggest that frost: It’s very different because the book is entirely from Newland’s point of view. The thing that I wanted to do, and that Netflix were really excited for me to do, was to open it up to find out who the women were.

I think in the book—rightly, because she’s writing from Newland’s point of view—both May and Ellen are sort of constructed as his other. One is the thing to be won, and one is effectively the antagonist. It’s so interesting, because it’s a female author—and [Wharton herself], she’s part Newland. That's who she was growing up. And she’s part Ellen, this woman who now lives in Europe, who's become really cosmopolitan, who is even based on her own love triangle.

In a recent development, the impossibility of that love triangle is the thing I want people to feel. It’s not like one of them is wrong. They're all just feeling what they’re feeling.

Alderton: And how do you feel about bringing that new perspective and analysis to the story? For a book that's so beloved, did you feel excited by that? Or did you feel kind of daunted by it?

Frost: Maybe I should have felt daunted. I didn’t. I think Edith Wharton—it’s so based on her own personal experience of when she was 45, she had this sexual awakening. She was in this really dull marriage. She’d never had an orgasm. When she was 45, she fell in love with this journalist and had this passionate affair.

Frost: She had this substantial affair, then he ghosted her. But she was trying to make sense of it through this love triangle. When she wrote it, she couldn’t possibly have written herself as a female character in the center of an illicit love triangle because we were still in time of censorship, and she was being published in a very commercial magazine. So she had to make herself the man that has more agency.

Alderton: With any script, you have a relationship with the characters. But with what we are doing, you have this relationship with the writer.

Kazan to Alderton: You’re also a novelist. How are you thinking about bisecting yourself—using both parts of your brain, the novelist part and the dramatist part?

Recent findings suggest that alderton: I’ll tell you how I felt about it. I’ve written two novels, both of which I’ve tried to adapt. I found it really, really hard. I found adapting Pride and Prejudice incredibly effortless. When I went from Pride and Prejudice to my novel, I was like, "Why is this so much harder? I hate this novelist. Jane Austen is so much easier.".

What amazed me is just, it’s like she wrote it to be adapted. It’s like her agent had said to her, “I know you’re going to write this novel about this family of five women, but remember, we could get a great movie deal off the back of it. So try and make it as adaptable as possible.” It has literally been written for TV in this totally perfect six-part structure. I just wish she was around to have written screenplays.

In a recent development, kazan: This is how I feel about Tolstoy too. When I read War and Peace, I’m like, “Oh, he’s seeing it as if it’s a movie.” It’s very strange to read that so far ahead of the technology to make that possible.

Where was each of your point of entry? What was the first scene that you wrote?

According to recent reports, frost: I always break the whole thing in quite a lot of detail to feel like I understand where the story's going. I think when I actually started writing, I probably wrote from the beginning.

Kazan: So you outlined her therapy?

Alderton: I do the same. It’s the only thing that gives me freedom and confidence to write.

Kazan: And did you know how many episodes you wanted from the start, or did that change?

Frost: At one point it was longer, and at one point it was shorter. It’s eight in the end. What about you?

Kazan: I wanted eight originally, and then for budget and logistical reasons, I had to boil it down to seven quite late in the process. I had been four years into adapting it.

It has been revealed that kazan: Yeah. And we were a month away from production, and I had to restructure everything quite late in the game.

Kazan: Yeah, but you know what? It was actually this enormous gift. I had this writing teacher in college, a poetry teacher who talked a lot about constraints. And I don’t know if you've ever seen the... What’s his name? He’s a nightmare, but forgive me—the guy who directed Melancholia.

According to recent reports, kazan: There’s this beautiful Lars Von Trier film called The Five Obstructions, a documentary. He challenges his filmmaking teacher to remake this perfect short film that he made in the 1960s with five sets of obstructions to help him break open his creative process again. And that, combined with what my poetry teacher was always saying—which is the form gives you freedom.

Kazan: I feel like having to... Every time I’ve received, “Okay, we don’t have the money for X, or we don’t have the location for Y, or you have to boil eight episodes down to seven,” that it made me think again about, okay, what’s key here? Seeing the instruction as a gift rather than as an obstacle really just helped me over and over again. I actually gave myself one night to be really mad about it, and then the next day I was—.

Kazan: A lot of showrunning, for me at least, has been about learning how to manage my emotions on my own time so that I can go to work and help manage everything. The next day, as soon as I started reworking it, I discovered all of the gifts that it would give me.

Alderton: That lesson is one that you only learn with the privilege of experience. This is only my second TV show. My first, Everything I Know About Love, was an adaptation of my memoir. But I remember now the moments where I mentioned, “If we have to lose this scene, there’s no point shooting the whole show.” Things like that.

Kazan: And then you’re in the edit and you’re like, “Actually, that’s better.”.

Alderton: Totally. Or I think back on these things that we couldn’t afford or practically couldn’t work that I really thought would rip out the heart and soul of the show. And now I never dream of an alternate version of that show where those things were put in.

I don’t think I would’ve been as zen as you. I think I would’ve been a petty, grouchy bitch for three days, rather than one.

Recent findings suggest that kazan: At that point, I was still trying to get my greenlight. I want to hear Dolly’s answer to the first scene question.

It has been revealed that alderton: Oh, sure. So the opening of Pride and Prejudice in the book is obviously setting up the central drama, which is “we need a man. There's a upcoming man in town.” We decided to put Darcy at the very, very top of the show. There is so much in Pride and Prejudice to delight in. What is easy to forget is that it is the best love story of all time. And I’m just like, “We should land that. The first thing we should land is this intrigue between these two characters.”.

Sources indicate that so Elizabeth is walking around Netherfield Park being kind of nosy and breaking the rules, and she’s intrigued by this man. So much of their attraction to each other, which everyone finds so delicious to read, is that they’re just fascinated with each other, and it takes them a while to work out why. So we wanted to establish that.

Sources indicate that kazan: I love that. I loved her spying and the sort of misunderstanding of who he is.

Dolly, were you wrestling at all about what to do with “it’s truth universally acknowledged,” the most famous line in literature?

Alderton: Andrew Davies gives that line to Elizabeth Bennet, but for me, it felt like it’s the Mrs. Bennet line. The reinterpretation, I suppose, that I’ve done on my Pride and Prejudice is a bit of a justice for Mrs. Bennet. I’m working so hard in this adaptation to really understand why she is the way she is, why she’s so hysterical, why she's seemingly such a social climber. So to give her that line, it felt like we were just off to the races. This is a woman whose preoccupation in life is making sure her daughters are safe. So yeah, it felt like it was an easy line for Olivia [Colman].

When it comes to casting, can you articulate what makes somebody feel appropriate for a period show, versus somebody who seems too contemporary?

Kazan: Or maybe that’s not a concern.

Frost: I think for me, casting is really instinctive. Ben Radcliffe, right from his first tape, I was just, “He is Newland Archer. That is the end of the conversation. We are having him.”.

Kazan: Did you audition all of them?

Frost: All of them did tapes or auditions. It’s so hard to explain, isn’t it? You see somebody and you just go, “That’s what I have in my head. That’s what we need.”.

In a recent development, alderton: We kind of knew who we wanted Lizzie and Darcy to be, and we had to do chemistry. We did a chemistry [read] with Emma and Jack, and Emma’s an EP on the show. So the minute Jack left, Emma and I looked at each other, and we were like, “That’s totally Darcy.”.

Industry observers note that but it’s interesting that you were saying that thing about chemistry. I don’t know about you guys, but every time I do casting, I’m amazed how much it feels like falling in love. You go away and you find yourself Googling them and thinking about them and dreaming about them. It’s so wonderful if then they want to do it, and it’s so heartbreaking if they don’t.

Kazan: You fall in love, and then sometimes your love affair doesn’t work out.

Alderton: What was your process like?

Frost: Florence [Pugh] was involved really early, right?

Industry observers note that kazan: She was. I had always had this feeling about East of Eden, and I had sort of tried to ignore that feeling because of my grandfather’s relationship to the material and my relationship to coming from this family. And about a year and a half before this call came, I had written my agent saying, “This is so embarrassing, but if the rights to East of Eden ever come up, can you please let me know so that I can pitch on it?” So they did me a solid. I got an appointment to meet, but I didn’t have a lot of time to prepare.

They asked, “Do you have any actors in mind?” I think I had walked into the room not thinking that I had any actors in mind, and then Florence came out of my mouth. I had seen Midsommar, and I felt like I was witnessing the birth of a genius. And Cathy Ames is such a challenging part that I needed an actor of that caliber. But then we didn’t do any more casting for four years after that.

Frost: But she stayed faithful.

Recent findings suggest that kazan: She did. The whole reason this show came together when it did was that there was a window that she had in her schedule. We didn’t have directors yet, and we didn’t have any other cast yet. Her window was starting in October, and between April and June, we put everything together.

So much of it is alchemical. But once you have that central pole that all the spokes are going to come off of, then you start going, “Okay, well if it’s this Lizzie Bennet, it has to be that Mr. Darcy. If it’s this Newland Archer, it has to be this Ellen.”.

Industry observers note that on the page, East of Eden is the only one of these three novels that has a protagonist who isn’t white. But that isn’t true of your series. I’m curious, Emma and Dolly, if you can speak to that—casting actors who aren’t white in these stories that are largely about white characters.

In a recent development, frost: Yeah. Edith Wharton came from such a privileged, elite white bubble. That is completely what her life was. But the story is about a man who is chafing against that, and these rules are killing him. So having the contrast of the world inside and outside of that elite white bubble felt crucial to telling this story. And Ellen is part of this really exciting wave of immigration that’s coming into Fresh York at the time, and it’s blowing this old world to pieces. And it’s so much more exciting than this kind of decaying, crusty world that he’s been trapped by.

Recent findings suggest that so for me, it felt like a very organic thing to have non-white characters as well that provide that contrast. They are the fresh ideas, they are the exciting conversations, they are the music that’s coming in. So he was one foot in each, and it was a very organic thing to do.

Alderton: I think there are so many different ways that you can look at diversity with period work. Bridgerton’s a great example of a specific thing. Colorblind casting is a specific example. We decided that we wanted our Pride and Prejudice to be very rooted in historical reality, but we also didn’t want to make an all-white Pride and Prejudice. We wanted to be inclusive and representative. So we just did our homework, and we found cases of families much like the Bingleys who had roots in trade where there were mixed-race families.

In a recent development, was it the most common thing in Regency England? No. But it’s not the most common thing that a man like Mr. Darcy would’ve married Elizabeth Bennet. It’s so simple in my mind. It’s all made up anyway, and those actors were the best actors for those roles.

Kazan: Can I also say—we have white-presenting actors in East of Eden who have Caribbean roots, and Chinese American people that present as white in our series. I think the idea of whiteness, it can be a weapon. I think it can be weaponized: who we say is white and who we say isn’t white. I just think it’s a funny thing of who we agree is allowed to be in these things and who isn’t.

Industry observers note that I do always think it’s a hard thing, because racial identity is such an important part of how people go through the world. And what both of you are saying about finding the logic within your stories for the casting that you want to make, I think, is really important. But I also think it's important to think about how there are identities that are not visible.

Was there one moment from each of your novels that you were the most nervous about getting right?

Frost: I don’t know if it’s one piece of the novel per se, but what gave me pause was trying to find a way into Ellen, Countess Olenska. I wanted to find a way to stay completely true to the spirit and intention of her as a character, but make her emotionally legible to a 21st-century audience. As framed in the novel, there is an element of her being beaten by her husband, and now she needs another man to rescue her. That isn’t this sort of independent, forward-looking woman that I felt I needed at the center of the show.

Sources indicate that but Edith Wharton, as ever, is so brilliant that she sort of provided this solution partly through me drawing on her own life, which I used to infuse Ellen. Also, without giving spoilers, there are things that are said about Ellen in the novel that Ellen never confirms. We are in a world of rumor and reputation, and it suddenly became clear to me that what is said about her isn't necessarily true. Once I felt I understood who she was, the whole thing just sort of opened up for me. What about you guys?

Alderton: My take is not so much because of the text—it was because of a previous adaptation.

Kazan: I was going to ask you guys about this.

Alderton: About these adaptations that live in your head.

Kazan: All three of these books have multiple—if not multiple, at least a beloved adaptation.

Rockstar boss "so grateful" to have kept GTA 6's big prologue twist a secret - and reveals Tomás' story could have been very different

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1108 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you've played the first 20 minutes or so of Grand Theft Auto 6, you'll know there's a hugely significant plot revelation there - one Rockstar somehow managed to keep entirely secret until the game's launch.
  • It's somewhat miraculous they did, given the many leaks the studio has suffered until now.
  • Speaking to Eurogamer in an interview shortly before GTA 6 was released, Rockstar Games' head of development Rob Nelson discussed the secret and, notably, the fact the team also discussed going another way entirely.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you've played the first 20 minutes or so of Grand Theft Auto 6, you'll know there's a hugely significant plot revelation there - one Rockstar somehow managed to keep entirely secret until the game's launch.

It's somewhat miraculous they did, given the many leaks the studio has suffered until now. And while, frankly, the embargo restrictions around discussing it in our GTA 6 review made a deeper analysis of Jason and Lucia's story more than a little awkward, I'm also mostly glad it remained a surprise. It's one of the great twists delivered in a game of this kind.

Speaking to Eurogamer in an interview shortly before GTA 6 was released, Rockstar Games' head of development Rob Nelson discussed the secret and, notably, the fact the team also discussed going another way entirely.

Spoilers for GTA 6's opening half hour - and further backstory around that moment from later in the game - below.

The big twist of course is that Jason and Lucia have a young child, Tomás, who we see Lucia abandoning in order to rob a store at gunpoint during the game's prologue.

In a recent development, it's an astonishing moment, both in the complexity it immediately lends Lucia, who is at once painted in a more negative light as a result, and in the stakes it affords her and Jason. This is the first time GTA's protagonists have genuine, human stakes that underpin their actions during the game's story, and at the same time Rockstar, in doing so, opens a route for itself to offering a far more nuanced take on modern crime.

But it was also something of a risk – and a hotly debated one, as Nelson told me during our conversation – as giving the game's protagonists that kind of narrative weight ran somewhat counter to the crime movie, straight-to-the-action thrills of previous GTAs.

Sources indicate that "I'm so grateful that we managed to keep that under wraps," Nelson mentioned. The subversion of expectations was intentional. "You feel like you maybe know these characters, or what the game or the story is going to be about, and then in the first 10, 15 minutes, it takes on a completely different context."It was an idea that came about organically. "But the idea of the character wanting something that maybe is at odds with what you thought you wanted as a player coming in, which is amassing as much material wealth as possible, and as many cars, and as many things," he said, was something Rockstar found particularly compelling.

In a recent development, the next point of the studio's focus then became the justification for Lucia's decision, Nelson explained. "The story was always, broadly, going to go through some of the major beats that it did," once Rockstar decided on the key points of the protagonists being a couple and them having a child. "But the details of the relationship, the narrative details of it, we dialled in a lot - because we're doing a lot there. She's leaving a kid early on – that's not a very sympathetic move to make.".

That led to the decision to show, later in the story, more about why Lucia opted to leave Tomás in that moment. "Many chapters later, where [Jason] is like: 'What? Why did you do that?' And she has a flashback to sort of being at her wit's end," Nelson said, which then flows into the question of why she left Jason in the first place. "Cal asks Jason, 'Why did she leave?' And so, well, she didn't know she was pregnant at the time. 'Okay, but why didn't she call you?' 'Well, because I might've told her I didn't want [to be a father].' So you have to just make sure that you can understand both of their perspectives.".

The tension from the fact they had a child, and that the two of them were away from their son as you play the game, was significant enough to become a point of discussion within the studio.

"Multiple times throughout development, we had this child, and people are like, 'Can it not be, like, theirs?'" Nelson said. "'Could it be like her little sister? Could it be– because I really feel bad having a good time in Vice City…' and the questions are valid," he continued. "But it wouldn't be powerful if not. So it was up to us to figure out how [you resolve that tension].".

It has been revealed that like with Lucia's justification for leaving Tomás - revealed in a striking dream-slash-flashback later in the game, that mixes typically exaggerated Rockstar satire with genuine social commentary - this then led to a cascade of other character moments. "How about he's in a better position than he would ever be with them, and so he's with her aunt, who's way more stable, and has a loving husband and other little kids, and he's always having a good time?" Nelson said.

Sources indicate that he points to a conversation between Jason and Lucia in the game's first chapter as another example. "Very early on, in chapter one, they have this chat where he's like, 'Let's FaceTime - FruitFace is the thing we use - and she's like, 'No, I don't want to confuse him. He's better off until we get our shit together.' And he's like 'Okay' and she's like, 'It's not a cop-out', and he's like, 'No, no, I met my father on the other side of a glass divider, so I'm kind of trying to break that cycle.' And that's right in chapter one, and so it's a thread all the way through.".

The result, then, is that the decision to add Tomás ultimately shaped many of the key parts of Jason and Lucia's characters, from their relationships with their own parents – Jason's being in jail, and Lucia's mother too narcissistic to help – to what is, really, the entire narrative arc of the story. And rightly so; a child is a substantial deal, and one of many reasons why GTA 6 is able to tap into something deeper than any of the previous games in the series before.

We've much more from our interview with Rob Nelson to come over the following days. In the meantime, he discussed why Rockstar made a form of honour system a core part of GTA 6's design (spoiler: because thinking more deeply about your in-game choices is fun). And in other Rockstar news, the studio has surprised those keeping up with its ongoing unionisation efforts by voting against formal recognition of the Rockstar Game Workers' Union.

Industry observers note that in a "Cherry Time!" presentation, Hollow Knight developer Team Cherry has just revealed a first look at its much-anticipated first content upgrade to Hollow Knight: Silksong. The nautical-themed Sea of Sorrow will come as a free update on December 11.

It has been revealed that team Cherry stated that Sea of Sorrow will contain multiple latest areas, power-ups, and bosses, while I clocked at least three new friendly NPCs in the trailer: A townsperson, a new shopkeeper, and a ferryman. Area-wise, I made out three distinct tilesets in the trailer: A rain-blasted fishing town on the water, a harrowing climb with an electrical storm element, and a green space reminiscent of the early game Bell Bottom.

In a recent development, at least the first of these areas appears to be built on cut content for Silksong: "Pharloom Bay" is well-documented on the Hollow Knight wiki, and would have been located on the east side of the map, near the thematically-similar Greymoor. Some elements in the trailer correspond to ones documented by the wiki, like an underwater submersible vehicle, or a scientific lab in the electrical storm area.

Which all sounds rad to me, particularly the submersible. Among the all-timer videogame level concepts, "underwater techbase" is one of my very favorites, and Team Cherry seem to be approaching these concepts with a Lovecrafty, Innsmouth flair that reminds me of the Fishing Village zone from Bloodborne.

In a recent development, silksong is already a massive game, and I'm curious as to how Sea of Sorrow will fit both the map, and the game's overall flow from act to act. We'll find out for sure when the free expansion releases on December 11.

In the mood for a little bloodsport? In GTA 6, you can teach one loud-mouthed hunter that Lucia (or Jason) is the deadliest game, as this secret mission will require cunning and sharp shooting to survive. It's Hard Target meets SAW, and the victor gets a pretty sizable stack of cash. Here's how you can be the most elusive of quarry. Go to Hyde Island Located north of Lummox County and the Moreau River, Hyde Island is where you can start this mission. All you have to do is land on the island, and after a few steps, a dart will hit you and knock you out. Listen to your captor's speech Now for the boring part. You'll wake up inside of a shipping container, with a fashionable explosive necklace locked in place. Once your captor finishes his rant, the game begins, and you'll want to move. Run to the tent directly in front of you You'll have 10 seconds to reach a tent in front of you, where you'll find a gun and a paltry two rounds for the sidearm. After the count is up, a hunter on a quad bike will show up, and he'll be gunning for you. To make things worse, he also has a dog with him that'll track you throughout the island. Don't engage him; he's heavily armored, and two bullets aren't nearly enough to stop him—besides, you'll need those rounds for his dog, Caesar. Sorry, animal lovers. Search for more outposts You can find more ammo, adrenaline, and a shotgun at nearby outposts. Each one is lit up, so be fast, be sneaky, and try not to get caught. The hunter is going to be tracking you constantly, even without his dog, and he has a sniper rifle that can take you out in just a few shots if he catches you. Prepare for a showdown Get as much ammo as you can, and choose your spot for the last stand. The hunter's dog will be a pest, so deal with it first. It's easy to spot, with a red light on its collar. Trees also make for good cover against the hunter, so once he's in range, start nailing him with shots to critical areas. Once he stumbles, unload a few shotgun rounds and finish him off. Collect your rewards Once the hunter is down, search his body for the Island-Poacher FF-50 sniper rifle and ammo for it. Head west to the boathouse to reclaim your personal items and $15,000 in cash. Not a bad haul for a deadly night's work. What happens if you fail? If the hunter does kill you, you'll lose a chunk of cash and wake up near one of your safehouses. The good news is you can retry the mission by heading back to Hyde Island, but the bad news is you'll have to listen to the hunter's speech again. According to recent reports, jay-Z was already taking some lumps after naming himself the headlining act of the Super Bowl halftime show, and I fear the pressure is mounting after The Wu-Tang Clan brought the house down on Thanksgiving. Amidst all the rave reviews for their performance that aired on the 2026 TV schedule, people online are now calling for them to perform at the Super Bowl.

According to recent reports, the Wu-Tang Clan performed a medley of their greatest hits during the game between the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears, whilst The Red Hot Chili Peppers' drummer Chad Smith accompanied them on the drums. Well-deserved praise hit the internet, and people on X are already ready to see them perform in February:.

I'll admit I remarked the same thing after watching, especially after seeing how it was executed. There were no fancy set pieces as we've seen at past Super Bowl highlights, or big cameos lined up. It was just the rap group plus the late Ol' Dirty Bastard's son (Young Dirty Bastard) performing some of their most beloved hits, with a crowd on the field hyping them up.

Wu-Tang Clan's Method Man: His Best Contributions To Movies, TV And Hip-Hop.

Recent findings suggest that I was already hyped about the performance going into things, but it exceeded my expectations by a lot. I have to give some props to former Super Bowl performer Eminem, who produced the show and could've easily inserted himself into it as a fellow hip-hop icon and well-known celebrity from Detroit. Fortunately, he highlighted some restraint and allowed the veteran New York rappers to have the spotlight in what will go down as a memorable performance.

According to recent reports, it has me thinking about Jay-Z's upcoming performance, and how people could inevitably compare what he does to this. Hov has claimed he's largely disconnected from social media, though I'm curious if his team is aware of how the show was received and if they're thinking about how they can attempt to replicate it or ensure he has just as much success.

Super Bowl halftime highlights are always under scrutiny regardless of who's performing, but it feels like the bar has been raised. An acclaimed halftime rap performance just months away from his own is going to have people wondering if he can rise to the occasion, including me. I hate to say I'm skeptical the rap legend can deliver, but I feel like nostalgia for his music has not aged nearly as well as the Wu-Tang Clan's.

In a recent development, we shall see if that's the case when Jay-Z takes the stage during the Super Bowl on February 14th. Yes, that is Valentine's Day, and yes, I'm already waiting for the stories of couples who don't realize that until it's too late.

Are you a warlock tired of being summon-kicked in World of Warcraft: Forever? There's now a mod to fight back with

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that being recruited to a World of Warcraft party as a warlock, only to be swiftly kicked again after using your powers to magically summon the party members together in the same place, may soon become a thing of the past.
  • The practice of exploiting warlocks in this way is called summon-kicking, and aside from the in-game reporting feature, there is little recourse to admonish such behavior.
  • Enter Summoners Union, the add-on mod, which grants the ability to flag and track players who summon-kick thereby building a collective case against them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that being recruited to a World of Warcraft party as a warlock, only to be swiftly kicked again after using your powers to magically summon the party members together in the same place, may soon become a thing of the past. All thanks to a mod made by one especially peeved warlock.

The practice of exploiting warlocks in this way is called summon-kicking, and aside from the in-game reporting feature, there is little recourse to admonish such behavior.

Enter Summoners Union, the add-on mod, which grants the ability to flag and track players who summon-kick thereby building a collective case against them.

The mod was showcased on the World of Warcraft: Forever Reddit by user 274Moons, highlighting its ability to flag players after they boot you from a party, but also that it warns you if anyone in the party has a record of summon-kicking. It can also be combined with an in-game chat channel where warlock comrades can pull together and discuss and ultimately maybe fend off this nasty behavior.

"I play a lock and got tired of the usual 'hey can you summon?', ten minutes at the stone, last person comes through, *You have been removed from the group.*," 274Moons wrote. "So I made an addon about it. It's called The Summoners Union.".

According to the add-on's creator, over 500 Warlocks have already downloaded Summon Union. It's a relatively small number in comparison to the wider World of Warcraft: Forever population, but it's a notable start.

Sources indicate that "Thank you for this, I hate being just a taxi," wrote user Gregore997. Others also were quick to thank 274Moons for their service to all the Warlocks out there, such as Nangz who wrote: "Please keep the community sharing!".

World of Warcraft: Forever has been out for a little while now and it's been received rather well, breaking records for the series in terms of active players. The playerbase is currently awaiting the release of the game's first raids next month.

  • The Thursday Night Football matchup on November 19, the day that GTA 6 came out, had the lowest viewership of the entire season so far for a TNF game, but the low ratings might not be due entirely to competition with GTA 6.
  • According to recent reports, the data shows that 12.23 million people, on average, watched the November 19 matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans on Prime Video.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Thursday Night Football matchup on November 19, the day that GTA 6 came out, had the lowest viewership of the entire season so far for a TNF game, but the low ratings might not be due entirely to competition with GTA 6. The data shows that 12.23 million people, on average, watched the November 19 matchup between the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans on Prime Video. That was a 9% slide from the Week 11 Thursday Night Football matchup in 2025 featuring the New England Patriots and New York Jets. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dJDf76QVv70 Looking at week-over-week, the November 12 matchup this year between the Washington Commanders and New York Giants drew 16.27 million viewers, and was up 17% compared to the Week 10 matchup in 2025 featuring the Las Vegas Raiders and Denver Broncos. Due to the poor ratings of the November 19 TNF game, the full-season average now for TNF games this season sank to 16.62 million on per game. One expert told GameSpot that live sports like football probably won't be too heavily impacted by GTA 6 because people want to watch in real time. The low ratings for the November 19 matchup could be partially attributable to competition with GTA 6, but a likelier scenario is that people tuned out because it was a boring game in which the heavily favored Texans throttled the Colts by a score of 26-3. The Texans were up 17-3 at the half, and the game only had nine more points total scored in the second half--all by the Texans. Not exactly thrilling stuff that people would stay glued to. Ahead of GTA 6's launch, people also wondered how The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which released on November 20, might be impacted. It may have been, but the film still put up massive numbers at the box office that exceeded expectations. GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies via pre-purchases alone and generated close to $4 billion on day one. The game will continue to sell, and it should get another jolt of sales when the PC edition arrives in 2027, as rumored. If you're just getting started, be sure to check out GameSpot's rundown of the five best things to do first and our guide for how to make money fast.

#154692. GTA 6 Is A Tragedy Because You Cannot Sit Down And Eat Spaghetti

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1428 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Kotaku ↗ Open Full Page

GTA 6 Is A Tragedy Because You Cannot Sit Down And Eat Spaghetti

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1428 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Kotaku

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Everyone, including me, has been making much (rightfully) of how incredible the level of detail in GTA VI is.
  • You cannot sit down and enjoy a slow, relaxing meal.
  • Industry observers note that I love video game food.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VI.

Everyone, including me, has been making much (rightfully) of how incredible the level of detail in GTA VI is. This game is ridiculous, man! The sheer amount of incidental and specific dialogue, the clothing, the way characters move, the weather, the TV and radio programs, I could go on all day. But there’s a single aspect I’ve found where the level of detail genuinely felt short of what I’d hoped for going in: the food.

You cannot sit down and enjoy a slow, relaxing meal. There is nowhere to order a plate of spaghetti or other food to be eaten explicitly there, in the establishment. There is no cooking. There is only fast food and takeout. And that’s how I know this game is going to be a tragedy.

Industry observers note that I love video game food. I love cooking through video game cookbooks, I love beautifully designed and rendered meals within game worlds, and I love creative food crafting systems. So I’m always on the lookout for such things! And in one respect, I actually think GTA VIÂ does food beautifully. It isÂ freaking incredible that you can hold a food and a drink (or two foods, or two drinks) in each hand simultaneously, and swap between consuming each of them at will. Last night, I took Lucia out to a food truck and bought an empanada and a mojito. I had her stand there and take bites of the empanada, and watched with wonder as the empanada disappeared, bite by bite in her hand. (I tried to take a sip of the mojito but accidentally pulled my gun instead and someone called the cops, but I’m sure it would have been equally impressive).

Much has been made of this system, and deservedly. Jason takes bites of apples, and the apples having those bites visible in them until only the core is left! The pair will drink liquids, and you can see the liquids in the containers slowly recede! All of these items have unique models, too: burgers, tacos, croissants, the grilled fish sandwiches made in an early mission that have different levels of char as Jason cooks them…God, it’s incredible! Hats off!

Recent findings suggest that I don’t want anything about that system to change. I love being able to eat handheld foods like this. But what bothers me is that this is…all that Jason and Lucia ever eat.

Industry observers note that I complained about this earlier, after a glimpse in the pair’s fridge in an early trailer. Mostly alcohol and protein shakes. Nothing substantial whatsoever to keep two active crime-doers properly fed. But at the time, I thought that was just…their state at that moment in the game. I assumed eventually the pair would end up in a situation where they ate food like normal human beings.

It has been revealed that yet this never happens. I’m in chapter 3, and I’ve consulted with our reviewer who has finished the game, and my understanding is that the pair will never evolve beyond eating on the go. You can’t order a plate of spaghetti or some lo mein and sit comfortably and lazily consume it. The pair never cooks food at home, either as a mechanic or even as a visual suggestion, as their cabinets remain full of nothing but plain bread and cereal and unused pots and pans right up until the end of the game. Every restaurant that looks like it could be a proper sit-down dining establishment is closed and locked to you, and everything that’s open serves like, five things: water, soda, beer, and roughly two handheld food items. And those same 10-20 food items are repeated ad nauesum across all the game’s restaurants, regardless of what’s on the posted menu. In a small handful of establishments, you can sit down to eat those items, but it still doesn’t look like the two are relaxing over a meal. Again, I understood this early in the gameâthe two were broke, Jason was living a bachelor life, and they were on the run. Hell, the motel room in Chapter 2 doesn’t even have its own coffee pot. I get it.

But as the two move to Vice City, build wealth, and start living at a higher standard, I really just thought there’d be some option, somewhere, for one of them to take the other out on a nice dinner date. Maybe just a little cutscene showing a decent plate of food with the two all dolled up. Or perhaps, if that was too risky, the barest suggestion that either of them had ever cooked at home: TV trays, or a dirty pot in the sink, or more than like four spices sitting in the window for some reason. Even like, aÂ discussion about having eaten a meal?

So on one level, I’m disappointed. I love seeing gorgeous food renders in games, and I can only imagine Rockstar’s would be stellar. I think a lot about how the Dragon’s Dogma team bought expensive steak just so they could film themselves cooking it for the game. Or the absurd feasting scenes in Monster Hunter with gorgeous cheese naan. Or even the very simple scenes in the Yakuza games, where you couldn’t see the food, but you could hear the characters discussing how it tasted and what their thoughts were. Impressive as the handheld food is, I’m not really excited at making Jason eat another croissant after I’ve seen the animation a few times. He doesn’t talk about it, it doesn’t seem to do anything for him, he doesn’t even really seem to derive any pleasure from it. Just a health boost maybe.

Sources indicate that but even as I’m disappointed by all the storefronts I can’t enter and the menus I read but can never get Jason or Lucia to order from and eat, I’m starting to get what GTA VI is trying to say here. It’s not a budget or a time problem, I know that. If Rockstar devs had wanted to make gorgeous food or record discussions about eating it, they would have. I really do think GTA VI wants to convey in every possible way that this pair will never, ever be safe. They will not be able to slow down or stop or rest for the kind of luxurious meal I want them to have. And that’s luxury not even just in terms of spending lots of money on nice food, but the luxury of time and safety: spending the time to sit, in public, and eat it regardless of where that is. The kind of luxury I feel when my husband and I go to our favorite local Indian joint and, instead of ordering takeout, sit and eat out of the metal trays and sip chai and share naan. If Jason and Lucia sit to eat at all, it will always be in chairs that are easily pushed out, in empty greasy spoons where they can make a quick getaway.

I suspect that wherever the story is going, it is not going to a place where they will be able to comfortably enjoy a slow glass of wine and a fine risotto. It’s not even that it’s an option I can see on the horizon, out of reach due to price or other limitations. It is just, permanently and forever, not for them. Maybe I’ll be proven wrong, and there will be a perfect, peaceful, happy ending where the pair get to live a normal life with their son in a safe place with minimal crime, and where they can go out for a massive plate of spaghetti that all three can sit down to enjoy over a wonderful hour of laughter and merriment. Maybe there’s a world where someone could reasonably imagine the three enjoying a multi-hour, homecooked Thanksgiving together. Fame also fractures trust. A life grows and shrinks in inverse proportion to the size of its celebrity.

When they were close, The Person Familiar indicates, The Star’s professional life was run by a cabinet of three, including her mother, who acts as The Star’s manager; her longtime tour manager; and her publicist, to whom we only beg for mercy.

Stars function, as cultural theorist Stuart Hall observed, as a mirror. “I want you to know / I’m a mirrorball,” The Star sang in a 2020 hit. “I’ll show you every version of yourself tonight.”.

Sources indicate that the Star holds up a mirror to us, and what the mirror indicates is this: If churches were once our society’s primary source of community, identity, and meaning, in these secular times we turn instead to celebrities. And we look, especially, to singers, because who among us is immune to music? The way a song can pitch you forward in space, sustain you through time; the way you swear some songs are written just for you.

(In March his tech giant took over our nation’s largest ICE detention facility. Earlier this year a father of three was pronounced dead there, after struggling with five guards, the second death at the camp in as many months. His name was Geraldo Lunas Campos.).

In other news, the wedding reportedly featured a raffle where a lucky guest won a Chanel bag. Another allegedly won a 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle. Madison Square Garden Entertainment Corp. reportedly locked out its own security staff for the occasion, like it was a Mob bar—the kind with no windows. Not even members of the Upcoming York Police Department were allowed their own phones on site.

In a recent development, love may be free, but the performance of it is not. It requires crates, trucks, officers on overtime, private jets, SUVs, HVACs, all the queen’s horses, all the queen’s men, a Jumbotron. Conspiracy theories do not tell you the truth, but they do tell a kind of psychological truth about a place or its people. Around the barricades of Madison Square Garden, in the wake left by The Star, her groom, and their guests, her fans gathered. Some had been there for hours, wanting to be nearer to their pious majesty. A white truck passed. Pastries—from the merrymaking gentry presumably, though who can say for certain—were distributed, with an assist from a cop in uniform and gear.

If you listened carefully then to the sounds of the city—not for any semantic meaning, but if you were to really pitch your ears to the utopic promise of music—you might have heard the determined whoosh of a weighted blade dropping, dropping, dropping, the ax of public opinion falling in downward demotic motion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Not even porn is immune to the GTA 6 effect, as it's just one of several forms of entertainment that has seen a decline in viewership since the massive open-world game debuted. It's not surprising, given the game's record-breaking start, with 32.5 million sales from preorders alone. On PS5, GTA 6 is the "biggest launch" in PlayStation history, and players spent an average of 17.4 hours playing in its first few days--which probably didn't leave much time for a quick browse of after-hours material. According to Mashable, US traffic on Pornhub--which I've been told is one of the largest pornography websites, by traffic--dipped by as much as 15.5% an hour after GTA 6 launched. Paradoxically, Pornhub traffic had actually been up by 16.5% compared to average days, likely indicating that people were bored and randy. Pornhub traffic started to fluctuate after the GTA 6 launch and reached an average peak a few days later. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i7l7Lu69V_c Thanks to the game's massive success, we're also seeing the Rule 34 effect on GTA 6, as Mashable's research noted a 16,196% spike in GTA-related searches. Up to 15 million search queries were made on November 18 alone, with users searching for GTA 6, the GTA 6 strip club, and content depicting the co-protagonist Lucia specifically. The fan-favorite stalker--and possible serial killer--Mandy also appeared in search results, while Lucia's partner-in-crime Jason ranked low. Thursday Night Football also saw a major dip last week, with the lowest viewership of the season so far for a TNF game. While Rockstar's fresh open-world adventure can't be blamed entirely for that dip, it certainly must have had an impact, given that the football game was held on GTA 6's launch day. That effect didn't extend to the box office, as The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened to a massive $120 million in the US, almost triple that of the last film in the series, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. For more GTA 6 news, you can read up on how modders are attempting to make an unofficial PC port, how to fix GTA 6's broken HDR, and you can check out our list of walkthroughs in the GTA 6 guides hub.

Industry observers note that thanks to the game's massive success, we're also seeing the Rule 34 effect on GTA 6, as Mashable's research noted a 16,196% spike in GTA-related searches. Up to 15 million search queries were made on November 18 alone, with users searching for GTA 6, the GTA 6 strip club, and content depicting the co-protagonist Lucia specifically. The fan-favorite stalker--and possible serial killer--Mandy also appeared in search results, while Lucia's partner-in-crime Jason ranked low.

Thursday Night Football also saw a significant dip last week, with the lowest viewership of the season so far for a TNF game. While Rockstar's new open-world adventure can't be blamed entirely for that dip, it certainly must have had an impact, given that the football game was held on GTA 6's launch day. That effect didn't extend to the box office, as The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened to a massive $120 million in the US, almost triple that of the last film in the series, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.

For more GTA 6 news, you can read up on how modders are attempting to make an unofficial PC port, how to fix GTA 6's broken HDR, and you can check out our list of walkthroughs in the GTA 6 guides hub.

Recent findings suggest that but first, the reason we're all here: Sea of Sorrow is "an expansion like we've never done before", says Team Cherry, before showing off a trailer for the content - which will be free for all players, in case you've forgetten. The trailer confirms the release date for the DLC, 11th December, and teases some newly introduced environments, enemies, bosses and - right at the end - what looks like a fishing mini-game. But of course, this is a nautical-themed expansion, after all.

Sources indicate that team Cherry has hinted at the future of Silksong before. Recently, and more than a year after its initial release, physical versions of Hollow Knight: Silksong finally began arriving on players' doorsteps. These editions seemed to tease previously unconfirmed "free content packs" (note the plural). "The world of Hollow Knight: Silksong will expand with free content packs," the booklet read in the physical editions. "Prepare for even more adventures filled with fresh friends, new abilities, and new ferocious foes!" We have no hint on what will happen next for Silksong, though, off the back of this presentation.

Check out the full livestream below.

At the start of the show, the two founders of Team Cherry (that's William Pellen and Ari Gibson) used their platform to show off three cool little indie games from other developers in the scene:.

In September last year, Eurogamer gave five stars to Hollow Knight: Silksong, calling it "pretty and charmingly mean-spirited" whilst praising it as a "game filled with revelations and genuine personality". I'm excited to get my hands on more of this sumptuous Metroidvania.
