📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that as we approach the holiday season, we also approach the time when we all need to start buying gifts for people we know. Sometimes this can be annoying, but this year, if you have someone in your life who’s playing a ton of Grand Theft Auto 6 (and considering how many copies it’s sold, there’s a good chance you do!), there are some really easy gifts you can get them that will make them almost as happy as hanging out with Jason and Lucia.

Here are 11 gift ideas for the GTA 6 fan in your life. Just remember to figure out which console they’re playing on so you don’t get the wrong version of some of these gifts.

In a recent development, assuming the GTA 6 fan in your life is playing on PS5 which, statistically speaking, is very likely, this is a fantastic option for them. Any version of this controller looks great and will let them explore Vice City in style.

Xbox doesn’t have an official GTA 6 controller, but you can find a really nice pink controller on sites like Amazon and Walmart. Just make sure you’re buying an officially branded Xbox controller and not some cheap knock-off that won’t feel good to use and will likely break after a few weeks. I’ve heard good things about this PowerA Vice City-inspired controller, but it uses a dongle or wire to connect, so keep that in mind.

Rockstar sells a variety of Grand Theft Auto 6 merch, like shirts and hats, on its official online store. If you aren’t sure what to get, I’ve got some of this stuff already, and I can easily recommend the tote bags. They’re well made, look cool, and are big enough to actually be useful while out and about. The shirts are also well made, but sizing runs small, so keep that in mind.

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto 6 has some incredible music in it, and many of the game’s tracks were created just for GTA 6, includingÂ the banger opening song “Starting From Zero.” Any GTA 6 fan is going to be listening to these songs on repeat for some time, so why not buy them a nice version of the album? Sure, you can listen to it digitally, but for the real GTA 6 fans out there, owning a physical copy of the album will be a treat. And if they’re into vinyl, you can buy them this awesome-looking version of the GTA 6 album.

Speaking of physical copies of the game, perhaps buy them a boxed copy of GTA 6. It’s true, it doesn’t come with a disc, but if they bought the game digitally, they don’t have a physical object to hold onto. They also don’t have a cool paper map, either. And if you want, you can just take the code from inside; they don’t need it, so you can keep it for yourself if you’ve yet to buy GTA 6.Â.

Industry observers note that they might already have the game, but they might not have purchased the $100 version of GTA 6. So figure that out, and if they haven’t, buy them a $20 PSN or Xbox card so they can upgrade to the Ultimate Edition and check out all the extra cosmetic goodies available in-game.

In a recent development, admittedly, this isn’t the best way to play the original Vice City. But it is a very easy way to play the original Vice City. And the GTA 6 fans in your life might be craving a trip to the original Vice City right now. With the Definitive Edition, which includes GTA 3, Vice City, and San Andreas, they can easily play the older games on the console and TV that they play GTA 6 on already. So while these remakes weren’t perfect, they’re convenient and can be bought physically, so you can wrap them up and pop them under the tree.

After playing a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6, I wanted to re-watch some classic crime movies. And at the top of my list were two all-timers set in Miami: Scarface and 2006’s Miami Vice.Â These can be found on Blu-ray pretty easily. If the GTA 6 fan in your life owns a PS5 or Xbox Series X console with a disc drive, you can buy them the 4K UHD version of Scarface. And next month, Miami Vice finally gets a director’s cut 4KUHD release. Perfect timing.

Industry observers note that yeah, sure, it’s not a GTA game, but Watch Dogs 2 is the closest Ubisoft ever got to matching the level of detail and fun found in actual Grand Theft Auto games. Plus, the game’s storyline about tech companies going too far and hackers fighting themselves and each other feels more relevant in 2026 than ever before.

Sources indicate that if the GTA fan in your life loved the grounded storytelling and realistic characters of GTA 6, then I’d recommend buying them Mafia: The Old Country on their platform of choice as a gift. Mafia: The Old Country is a shorter game than GTA 6, but it offers up some truly impressive visuals and a solid story about the old mafia in Italy and how dangerous, but alluring, it could be to those wanting a better life.

Sources indicate that hey, I own a few of these, and I love them so much. And after playing GTA 6, I’ve been busting them out of my closet when going to the store. So why not support your GTA 6 fan’s desire to live in Vice City and buy them a nice Hawaiian shirt? You can even find places selling knock-offs of Tommy Vercetti’s iconic blue Hawaiian shirt if you look around.

This is a gift that only works if they own a PS2 or a PS3 that can play PS2 games. But if they do, then maybe pick them up a copy of Vice City Stories on PS2. This is a somewhat rare GTA in 2026, as Rockstar never ported it to any other platforms after it launched on PSP, so outside of emulation and some in-development fan PC ports, the only way to play VCS is on a PS2. The game is also a bit hard to find these days, so just owning a copy of it is pretty cool. A lot of GTA fans have never played this game and might have forgotten about it at this point. This will get you plenty of cool points on Christmas.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CI Games has announced that Lords of the Fallen II is coming in April 2027, meaning it's been delayed again. An exact release date will be announced in December, the company said, and people are theorizing that could mean the date will be announced at The Game Awards on December 10. Lords of the Fallen II was originally scheduled to launch in 2026, but CI Games delayed it to Q1 2027 (January-March) to avoid GTA 6 and give the team more time to polish the experience. Now it's delayed to Q2 2027. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EYYXsH-DBoo For the previous delay, CI Games said feedback and tests revealed that there are “meaningful opportunities” available to “further refine and strengthen the overall experience” with more time. Despite its name, Lords of the Fallen 2 is actually the third game in the series, following Lord of the Fallen (2014) and Lords of the Fallen (2023). Based in Poland, CI Games is also known for the Sniper: Ghost Warrior series, the latest entry being 2021's Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2.

CI Games has announced that Lords of the Fallen II is coming in April 2027, meaning it's been delayed again. An exact release date will be announced in December, the company stated, and people are theorizing that could mean the date will be announced at The Game Awards on December 10.

In a recent development, lords of the Fallen II was originally scheduled to launch in 2026, but CI Games delayed it to Q1 2027 (January-March) to avoid GTA 6 and give the team more time to polish the experience. Now it's delayed to Q2 2027.

For the previous delay, CI Games mentioned feedback and tests indicated that there are “meaningful opportunities” available to “further refine and strengthen the overall experience” with more time.

Despite its name, Lords of the Fallen 2 is actually the third game in the series, following Lord of the Fallen (2014) and Lords of the Fallen (2023).

Based in Poland, CI Games is also known for the Sniper: Ghost Warrior series, the latest entry being 2021's Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Florence Pugh is one of the biggest movie stars we have right now. I mean she’s in both films bearing the Dunesday nickname on the 2026 movie schedule for crying out loud! So, I’d expect a director to move mountains in order to get her on their film. It turns out Pugh had balls of steel even before she earned her A-list status. When she was just 22, she was faced with the ultimate Sophie’s Choice of movie roles.

If you were to ask me what two Florence Pugh movies turned her from a burgeoning talent into a one of my favorite actors alive, I’d say it was the one-two punch of her portraying Dani in Midsommar and playing Amy March in Little Women back in 2019. As it happens, those are the same two films that she almost had to pick between. Pugh shared what it took to land both, recently, and I had no idea.

According to recent reports, I knew in my gut that I had to do both. And, I knew that if I let one of them go, I would regret that decision for the rest of my life. I called both directors with a significant ball of nerves in my stomach because I really wasn’t at the stage of my career where I should be calling a director and telling them that they need to reschedule their shoot, but I did.

Sources indicate that this, ladies and gentleman is yet another reason why Florence Pugh is the major name she is. She clearly understood at the time that she had stumbled onto two incredible parts, and she didn't want to choose, despite others telling her she must. With that in mind, she pushed aside any fears and decided to simply ask for what she wanted. Here’s what happened next, per her interview with Elle:.

In a recent development, I remember just telling myself like, ‘This is really hard. This is going to require for you to be very brave, but you need to do this because if you don’t you’ll regret not trying.’ And I did, and they made it work. So, I’m grateful for that.

It has been revealed that pugh ended up shooting Midsommar first with writer/director Ari Aster, which proved to be a taxing shoot for the actress. It was all worth it because the A24 film has since become known as one of the best horror movies of all time, with Dani’s May Queen and the Bear also becoming a popular Halloween costume, too. Pugh later also got a Midsommar tattoo to immortalize the movie on her body.

According to recent reports, right after she made Midsommar in Hungary, Pugh ventured to Massachusetts to make Little Women with writer/director Greta Gerwig alongside a cast including Timothée Chalamet, Saoirse Ronan, Emma Watson, Laura Dern and Meryl Streep. Whew, what a list! Little Women went on to give Pugh her first (and still only) Oscar nomination for Best Supporting Actress. Oh, and it also changed how we think about Amy March being a villain in the literary classic, probably forever.

While it feels like the absolute correct order for Pugh to have shot the films, she has spoken about getting depressed after coming home from the leftover Midsommar feelings she had “shelved” when making the joyful book adaptation about sisters.

Pugh's story goes to show, sometimes you just need to ask for what you want, and maybe you’ll get it! It’s particularly a good anecdote for people who might think they need to “earn” the right to request something, when that’s not always the case! And thank goodness she did, because her roles in Midsommar and Little Women are and will always be all-timers for her.

In a recent development, EA Motive's Iron Man game has been quietly cooking away for a few years now, but don't worry. The wait to finally, officially see the superhero romp in action might be over soon, at least if the developer's updated website - two weeks before The Game Awards, no less - is any indication.

Industry observers note that redditors today noticed that EA Motive's official website got a little makeover recently. It's not clear when exactly the tweaks were pushed through, but the Wayback Machine makes clear that it's definitely been updated.

A newly introduced website look is by no means confirmation of an imminent announcement, of course, but there are a few other bits of evidence that certainly point in that direction.

Recent findings suggest that for one, The Game Awards 2026 will air on Disney Plus for the very first time, alongside all the other platforms you're used to. "As the evening unfolds, viewers can expect major announcements and surprises from some of Disney's most anticipated titles in gaming," the film studio said earlier this month.

Kingdom Hearts 4, Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra and more are definitely possible, too. Turmoil at Marvel's Blade developer Arkane Lyon makes that one a tricker guess, however.

It has been revealed that second is the fact that The Game Awards air on 10th December - eight days before the global opening of Avengers: Doomsday, a film that's shaping up to become the biggest cinematic event since the last time Marvel chucked all of its toys into the same sandbox and bashed them together. Giving one of the company's most popular superheroes the spotlight around the same time seems like a good idea.

This isn't the first time EA's Iron Man has popped up in recent times, either. What appeared to be an unfinished trailer for Motive's Iron Man leaked onto the internet this summer, and showed off blisteringly fast flying and lots of destructive gadgets. It looked further along than I expected, at least, so I wouldn't be surprised to see the billionaire playboy philanthropist rear his head again in two weeks time.

Another Gaming Console Price Hike Could Be Coming, Thanks To Latest Tariffs

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (723 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The US government has revealed a new round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners.
  • According to recent reports, the US government has revealed a new round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners.
  • In a recent development, what does this mean for gaming hardware?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The US government has revealed a new round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners. Under the proposed tariffs, import taxes will rise significantly, with China facing up to 40% when the new duties take effect next year. According to the BBC, some of the rates will be reduced because of tariff caps that US President Donald Trump has already agreed to, and individual countries could also face different levies. What does this mean for gaming hardware? Trump's first round of "Liberation Day" tariffs contributed to rising console prices, but the Supreme Court eventually struck them down. Big companies like Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo benefited from tariff refunds after the ruling, but they didn't pass the savings on to consumers. In Sony's case, it was estimated to get back $508 million in refunds from the US government. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY&t=19s The new tariffs bypass the Supreme Court's ruling by using a different law, Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the government to impose tariffs on countries that use unfair business practices. The law does require an investigation into specific trade practices before rates are set. If higher import taxes take effect, console companies could face much higher costs, and protecting their profits will likely mean consumers have to cover the difference. Nintendo, Sony, and Microsoft have moved much of their final assembly out of China and into Southeast Asia, especially Vietnam, to avoid earlier tariffs. However, key parts like batteries and power supplies still mostly come from China, and if tariffs on these parts rise, total production costs for consoles made outside China will go up even more. Some electronic goods could be exempt from tariffs, and manufacturers often stockpile inventory ahead of tariff deadlines to delay price changes. But with rising costs from the ongoing components shortage amid the AI boom and other global factors, console prices remain at risk. After the June announcement of steep console price hikes, Microsoft warned that Xbox console costs could rise again in 2027, and next-gen hardware is also expected to be very pricey.

The actor who plays Mandy, Lexie Shoaibi, has now discussed how she got the part and her reaction to people being weird online. Speaking to Vulture, Shoaibi said she's able to see "more good than bad" thanks to her experience being a content creator. "There are weirdos out there, and they’re going to try to bring you down, so it’s important to stay around the people and the places that aren’t doing that," she said. "It’s easy enough to do, which I’m very grateful for. There’s enough support in my real-life community and online that I can say, 'I could just hang out over here. I don’t actually need to go to the scary place.' I’m living in the positive, for sure." https://www.youtube.com/shorts/JSJwQthWrZs People have been, to put it mildly, thirsting over Mandy since GTA 6 came out. However, Shoaibi had no idea she was going to be in GTA 6 at all because when she auditioned, she signed what she described as an "incredibly" strict NDA. In fact, she didn't even know what she was auditioning for. Her commercial agent in Fresh York brought it to her, and she thought it would be "just like any other commercial audition." From the time she auditioned until the game rolled out on November 19, Shoaibi did not know she was going to be in GTA 6. Instead, she did the audition and recorded her scenes for a project she knew as "Project Bubblegum." Shoaibi said the notes she received included being told to play a “sexy ex-girlfriend" and to "be seductive.”  When Shoaibi finally saw Mandy in GTA 6, she said it was "very exciting," in part because it meant that Rockstar didn't cut it. She did the recording for Mandy in 2023 or early 2024, Shoaibi said, and now that GTA 6 is finally here and her role as Mandy confirmed, Shoaibi said, "I feel like I'm living in a dream. It's crazy." Shoaibi said she hopes her role as Mandy in the biggest video game ever can help grow her profile and get more jobs. "There’s definitely momentum that I wasn’t feeling before," she said. GTA 6 launched on November 19 and had a gigantic debut, selling 32.5 million copies by launch and generating around $4 billion on day one. 📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coros has unveiled the Vertix 4, an “expedition-focused” revision to the Vertix 2 and 2S.
  • This watch is being marketed as a major step up from the Vertix 2S, with an AMOLED display, a more refined design, satellite maps and, for the first time on a Coros watch, a built-in flashlight.
  • In a recent development, that price does still undercut the latest Garmin Fenix 9 line-up, which starts at $999, though some rivals are cheaper still.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coros has unveiled the Vertix 4, an “expedition-focused” revision to the Vertix 2 and 2S. Coros indicates it pairs the brand's brightest display yet with long battery life, and after unboxing it myself, I can definitely say it has a more refined feel that could indeed suit the office as well as the summit.

This watch is being marketed as a major step up from the Vertix 2S, with an AMOLED display, a more refined design, satellite maps and, for the first time on a Coros watch, a built-in flashlight. The Vertix 4 will be available to buy starting on Black Friday, Nov. 27, but it won't exactly be at a discount: It costs $799, a $100 increase over the Vertix 2S.

In a recent development, that price does still undercut the latest Garmin Fenix 9 line-up, which starts at $999, though some rivals are cheaper still. For instance, the Suunto Vertical 2 steel model costs $599, and the Garmin Fenix 8 is at the moment on sale for $749.99 at Amazon.

I've only just started testing the Vertix 4 and haven't even had enough time to get through its substantial battery life, but I can share some first impressions, particularly in how it compares with the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro that launched earlier this year.

Recent findings suggest that built-in flashlights have become a must-have feature on premium sports watches, and now the Vertix 4 is the first Coros watch to get one. Coros has departed from the usual layout, though. Garmin, Suunto and Amazfit put the light on top of the watch, but Coros places it on the side, between the digital dial and the back button.

According to recent reports, previous Vertix watches used a memory-in-pixel (MIP) display. MIP has advantages, most notably longer battery life, but I know I much prefer the vibrant display on AMOLED screens, like on the Vertix 4. It is the biggest visual change and a large part of why the watch looks more premium than its predecessors.

Coros claims up to 30 days in watch mode, or 10 days with the screen always on. It also quotes 48 hours of multi-band GPS tracking with the screen always on. I haven't had time to test these claims properly, so stay tuned.

Coros watches are high-quality sports watches, but don't expect to find all the little lifestyle features you've come to expect on a more traditional smartwatch:.

Music: It can store tracks, but only files you drag and drop onto the watch. It doesn't pair with streaming services.

Payments: There is no NFC payment support.

Watch faces: Customization is more limited than on rivals.

On paper, the Vertix 4 looks like a significant upgrade: a better display, a more attractive design, a flashlight and satellite maps, at a price well below the Fenix 9 line-up. The $100 increase and cheaper alternatives like the Suunto Vertical 2 and discounted Fenix 8 will matter to some buyers, as will the limited smart features.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • “If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that prince William is reportedly actively considering a plan for a “far-reaching restructuring” of the British monarchy, which he would implement once he ascends to the throne. His brother, Prince Harry, would be at the forefront of these changes: The future monarch reportedly wants only active members of the royal family who carry out duties on his behalf to retain their royal titles and the style of “Royal Highness.” These titles would therefore no longer be an “automatic privilege of birth” but would instead be equivalent to a “job title.”.

It has been revealed that the plan was detailed by Tom Sykes, a journalist and writer specializing in the royals, in his book Dukes of Hazard, to be published next February, excerpts of which were published by the Mail on Sunday on Saturday, November 21. The author, “a royal authority with impeccable society contacts” as the newspaper puts it, is said to have obtained confessions from friends of Prince William.

“If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title. You will also get an allowance, a salary, and a place to live. One place to live,” the associate of the prince explained to Sykes. “If you are not doing those things and you are not a working royal, you will not get to be an HRH, you will not get a free or subsidized place to live, and you will not get any special favors. You will, however, be a private citizen free to get on with your life and make money any way you choose.”.

By implementing this measure, Prince William hopes to prevent potential media scandals regarding the legitimacy of certain individuals’ right to retain their titles if they are not prominent members of the Firm (Prince Harry) or if they are under legal scrutiny (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor). But also, and above all, the Prince of Wales hopes to offer an option to his children, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight, who could easily renounce their titles to pursue independent careers. The question does not arise for the eldest child of the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince George, 13, whose future as heir to the throne is “guaranteed.” In fact, none of the three use their royal titles, preferring simply to be called by their first names and the surname Wales.

It has been revealed that under the rules established by King George V in 1917, the title of prince or princess, along with the predicate, is granted at birth to the sovereign’s children and to the children of the sovereign’s sons, as well as to all the children of the Prince of Wales’s eldest son. Prince William’s children, therefore, received these titles at birth, while Prince Harry’s children, Archie and Lilibet (ages seven and five), did not become prince and princess until King Charles III ascended the throne.

Recent findings suggest that they may have to give them up if Prince William carries out his strategy. “Under William’s current plan, the prince and princess titles of Harry and Meghan’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, would be legally removed, along with the royal styles and princely titles of Harry and Meghan themselves,” writes Tom Sykes in his book. To do so, according to Sykes’s book, constitutional advisers have told William that he could concern letters patent, an official document authorized by the king. Such a decision could strain the relationship between the two brothers.

Sykes is convinced that Prince William would garner the approval of his subjects and “enormous public support in a country increasingly impatient with the cost and perceived excess of a sprawling royal household,” according to those close to him.

Recent findings suggest that in October 2025, Prince William confided to actor Eugene Levy—whom he was hosting at Windsor Castle for the taping of Levy’s show The Reluctant Traveler—that “there are points when you look at tradition and go, Is that still fit for purpose today? Is that still the right thing to do? Are we still doing and having the most impact we could be having?”.

Kensington Palace, however, declined to comment on the rumor. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on books or claims made within them.”.

Diablo 4 Is Making Helltides A Hell Of A Lot Easier

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (825 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, one of Diablo 4's oldest endgame activities, Helltides, is getting a major refresh for Season 16.
  • One of Diablo 4's oldest endgame activities, Helltides, is getting a major refresh for Season 16.
  • As detailed by developer Blizzard in their full breakdown of Season of Tyrael's Gambit, Helltides will soon be far more efficient to run than before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, one of Diablo 4's oldest endgame activities, Helltides, is getting a major refresh for Season 16. As detailed by developer Blizzard in their full breakdown of Season of Tyrael's Gambit, Helltides will soon be far more efficient to run than before. The whole point of the activity is to kill as many demons as fast as possible, acquire the Aberrant Cinders they drop, and then use those cinders to open chests for items. Dying means losing half of the cinders you've collected, but they are also lost when the Helltide ends. Oftentimes that means having left over amounts of cinders you can't spend, only to then go to the next Helltide five minutes later and repeat the process from zero. It's been this way since Diablo 4 debuted back in 2023. https://www.youtube.com/live/zhsLeug_ooo?si=EeprZXb-pEZ_KRiQ In Season 16, that will finally change. Blizzard is getting rid of the downtime between Helltides spawning and making it so there will always be a Helltide up in one of the game's original zones, as well as one in expansion areas like Hahantu or Skovos. Even better, Aberrant Cinders won't be lost once a Helltide ends. Instead, players can collect up to 5,000 cinders at a time to be spent on opening chests within the activity. Additionally, the overall loot quality from opening chests in the Helltide will be improved and chests can be opened instantly. Those changes should go a long way towards making Helltides feel more valuable and efficient when trying to farm gear, as you can now blast demons to your heart's content until reaching the Aberrant Cinder cap. Just don't die while you have a full 5,000 stored up. Diablo 4 Season 16 rolls out December 1. Alongside its Helltide changes, the season will bring big updates to War Intends as well. A new system, War Plans Tactics, will give players more control over what activities appear in their War Plans, as well as more options when it comes to rerolling them and the rewards they grant. Players will also have new Horadric items to chase that will modify specific Talisman sets, greatly increasing their power. Blizzard additionally announced many of the features that were added as part of Diablo 4 Season 15, Hell's Legacy, will be made permanent. Those additions include the season's capstone dungeons, optional bosses like Moophisto, the Annihilus Seal, Hellfire Torch Charm, and the season's legacy Unique items like Stone of Jordan.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that DFor centuries archaeologists have attempted to learn the origins of what we believe was known as Bleak Friday. Theories have long-pointed toward some sort of national purge day, in which citizens of the United States were encouraged to murder one another in the pursuit of widescreen televisions. But more and more evidence is being unearthed that it might have been a day of mourning due to not knowing which indie game to play next. To prevent a repeat of such a tragic era of human history, we at Kotaku 3000 are introducing preventative measures, and have compiled together 12 completely excellent lesser-known indie games to keep the bleakness away.

According to recent reports, or indeed, I asked developers to email me about their recently released or upcoming games that aren’t getting any attention, so I could stick them on the front page of the site while the bosses are distracted by sales. 12 such games went up on the site yesterday, and here are 12 more! I really cannot get over the incredible variety, originality and excellence on display here. Some are already out and can be bought, and the rest deserve a place on your wishlist.

Developer: Pandan Games Release date: Q2 2027 Steam.

An indie game inspired byÂ Ratchet & Clank is a tall order, but it really looks like Pandan Games could do it.Â GearGrit is a third-person platformer where you play as Tansy Geargrit, escaping from prison for crimes she maybe only committed some of, and attempting to unearth a giant government conspiracy.

Developer: darqwerful Release date: TBA Steam.

Detective games are having such an excellent resurgence, andÂ The Detective’s Apprentice looks to be offering a deep, pure example of the form. You play as Cleo, the niece of famous detective Maya Lynch, searching for clues and making logical deductions to solve crimes and murders. Thematically it looks to be of an Agatha Christie era, with all sorts of crime reconstruction, interviewing, information gathering, and all that good stuff. There is a demo, although no release date yet.

Developer: Sebastian Gioseffi Release date: Out now Steam.

“A very short game about the very best part of video games: the menus,” reads the store description forÂ Video Game Menu: The Game. And boy, does it have a lot of menus. Menus with buttons! And toggles! And an option for “cursorphobic buttons.” There’s also an option for “looming figure” which seems a bit unsettling. And apparently a way to get a flight sim HUD. It looks wonderfully bonkers, and you can buy and play it right now.

Developer: Mothman Mothman Studios Release date: Out now Steam.

I suppose you could argue thatÂ PokÃ©mon Snap is a form of cryptid cam game, butÂ CryptidCam is the real thing. This super-cute game is about taking photos of sweet little woodland oddities, including the likes of the Loch Ness Monster, bigfoot, and the Loveland Frogman (my latest obsession), as well as just gorgeous beasties with extra horns. You add your photos to the Cryptid-Nomicon, all for the sake of mysterious cryptozoologist Dr. Ted Krupp, and enough of my waffle, it’s out now so I’m already installing it.

Developer: Chaparral Collective, Unspeakable Pixels Release date: 2027 Steam.

Sources indicate that unspeakable Pixels made 2020’s utterly wonderfulÂ Batbarian: Testament of the Primordials, and you should definitely go buy and play that immediately. Do that while waiting for next year’sÂ Gift of the Primordials, a turn-based puzzle game about…balancing soil nutrients? No, come back, it looks really good! It’s about building habitats for fantasy wildlife through puzzle mechanics based around judicious placement of plants. I’m still not selling it well. Watch the trailer. And playÂ Batbarian.

Developer: Sunna Entertainment Release date: TBA Steam.

Sources indicate that surely this can’t be the first time someone’s thought to crossÂ Tetris with a platform game? But I’ve certainly never seen it before. And hot-damn, check out the animation work in the trailer above. This just looks phenomenal, with multiple characters and loadouts, buildingÂ Tetrisy towers in order to attack enemies, build combos and gather new skills. There’s a demo to check it out right now, but no sign of a release date yet.

Developer: Gabriel Maldonado Release date: Dec 4 Steam.

Sources indicate that “Flash is fragile,” indicates the blurb forÂ Ad Iterum, “but you can hack it.” Eek. This top-down turn-based roguelike looks gloriously macabre, with wonderful pixel art, as you descend through dungeons mutating your own body through the devouring of your enemies. It’s about seeing how far down you dare go, before attempting to return to the surface with your ill-gotten gains, with unique combinations of mutations defining each run through the procedurally generated world. And it’s out next week!

Developer: Little Sister Games Release date: 2027 Steam.

Sources indicate that as we all know, the way through the underworld is not via well-timed combat, but through the rolling of dice.Â Lovers Die is a Yahtzee-inspired roguelite, rolling dice to eliminate categories as you build up attacks. I adore the art here, those crunchy pixels and the wonderful way descriptive text is presented. Also, why aren’t more dicebuilders based on Yahtzee?! This is a darker, more adult game that the art might initially suggest, and looks compelling. We have to wait until next year to play it.

Developer: Fe Angelo, 2dchaos Release date: TBA Steam, Itch.

Sources indicate that oh my goodness, you have to check out how this third-person survival horror uses color. It’s stunning. I mean, everything about the art is stunning.Â NechromiaÂ is about escaping a gothic castle built of someone else’s memories, with only a lantern to protect you. This looks so incredibly promising, and there’s a demo available on the Itch page for the game.

Developer: Dagada’s Team, Matthieu Lu Release date: TBA Steam.

Gosh, this immediately induced some nostalgia.Â Dagada’s Story looks deeply reminiscent of the Atari/Amiga era of 16-bit platformers, complete with a mascot-like main character. You play as Dagada and his flying chum Naou, able to control each separately in order to solve puzzles, with the goal of saving the harmony of an alien mountain in order to repair Dagada’s spaceship and get home. It looks very charming, and there’s already a demo to check out.

Developer: Stellar Cartography Interactive Release date: Out now Steam.

Industry observers note that is it OK to decide you already like a game entirely based on the pun in its title?Â Prophet MarginÂ is part city builder, part board game and part strategy, all about creating trade routes that please the gods. The emphasis is on calm, meditative play, with lots of deep thinking and methodical planning, as well as appeasing the deities of each resource. It came out just a few weeks ago, and for those who’ve discovered it is proving very well-received, although the unfortunate closure of the intended publisher means it’s not yet found enough eyes.

Developer: Goloso Games Release date: TBA Steam.

One-person team Goloso Games made 2021’s excellentÂ Inspector Waffles, a great point-and-click adventure that is well worth your time. Their next game isÂ Antenna Dilemma, a latest adventure featuring C432632, a grey cube who discovers there’s more to reality than his sofa and TV. It looks superbly bizarre, and there’s a demo out there already if you want to find out more.

According to recent reports, the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the organization introduced a upcoming model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

Recent findings suggest that if you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

If you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is right now $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

The upcoming Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

It has been revealed that if you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's currently pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

If you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, currently marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

In a recent development, if you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (at the moment $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

In a recent development, for about $30 more than the X4 Classic, you can upgrade to the Xteink X4 Pro, which happens to be Lifehacker's e-reader Gift of the Year pick. It offers all the perks of the other Xteink devices, with two critical quality-of-life upgrades: A touchscreen for easier navigation, and a temperature-adjustable front light so you can read it in a dark room. (Less obviously, it also has a slightly faster processor that makes the whole thing feel a little snappier.) Right now, the X4 Pro is at its lowest price ever when ordered directly from Xteink: $84, or around 15% off the usual $99 price.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, capcom has had a big year, but amid the hits comes news that its Overwatch-with-dinosaurs game, Exoprimal, will join the live-service graveyard next year. The game's servers will go offline next year, making it unplayable after that. "Thank you so much for your continued use of Exoprimal, a statement on the Exoprimal site reads. "We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of Thursday, September 30, 2027. We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement." Exoprimal season passes are no longer available to purchase through storefronts, and Capcom will slowly wind down the game over several months. Exoprimal and all its DLC will be delisted from stores starting March 30, 2027, but anyone who owns it can still download and play it before the September 2027 deadline. Despite a cool premise and fun gameplay, Exoprimal never truly took off after its 2023 launch. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MEIkK11k09U "While Exoprimal’s early hours of repetitive and simple missions will likely drive some people away, its later surprises are a delight for those willing to give it the necessary time," James Carr wrote in GameSpot's Exoprimal review. "The escalation of difficulty and the wide variety of objectives introduced later on in the shooter gives it fresh life several hours in. Fighting through an ocean of dinosaurs is a ton of fun, and the variety of enemies keeps you from falling into a repetitive combat loop." The writing was already on the wall for Exoprimal in 2024, as Capcom unveiled it was ending seasonal updates and would rotate through existing content on a monthly schedule. While that doesn't reflect the entire player community, Exoprimal numbers have largely cratered on PC via Steam: it peaked at 4,9995 concurrent players in November 2023 and nosedived the following month. At the time of writing, Exoprimal's 24-hour peak was a paltry 23 players. 2026 has been merciless for live-service games, with several high-profile casualties. Developer Wildlight’s free-to-play shooter Highguard swiftly lost momentum after its January launch, Anthem was sunset this year, and Fresh World: Aeternum began winding down operations ahead of its January 2027 closure.

The Prime Evil Council is also becoming permanent, and will work the same way the game's other Lair bosses do, with players needing a specific item to open their reward chest after successfully defeating the encounter. Waking Nightmare dungeons will still be accessible, but only by finding Chronicle of Nightmares dungeon keys. Monsters from previous Diablo games will also have a chance to spawn in The Pit. Those who progressed their secret cow level journey can also rejoice, as the secret cow island and its corresponding waypoint will be staying. Many of Hell's Legacy's best items were new versions of classics from older Diablo games, and those Legacy Uniques will be added permanently as well, including the Annihilus Seal and Hellfire Torch Charm. That's all for now, but Blizzard said more of Hell's Legacy could make a return in the future. "Other popularly requested features are being evaluated for rework and may appear in the future," Blizzard said. Diablo 4 Season 16 launches December 1. In addition to bringing forward much of Hell's Legacy, Tyrael's Gambit will additionally overhaul the game's War Plans system and make its Helltide activity easier. Diablo 4 won't receive new expansions going forward, but it is receiving a new class, the Amazon, next year. Blizzard is also hard at work on Diablo 5. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • The plot heavily involved a Texas abortion clinic, and the state had just passed SB 8, one of the country’s most restrictive abortion bills until Roe v.
  • “I started thinking about the ‘red state, blue state’ of it,” she tells Vanity Fair ahead of the show’s season two premiere on Thursday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2021, at the recommendation of a film producer, the writer and showrunner Rebecca Cutter read a pulpy murder-mystery novel on a flight from her native Massachusetts to her current base in Los Angeles. By the time she landed, Cutter had finished the book and was already mapping out the TV adaptation in her head.

The plot heavily involved a Texas abortion clinic, and the state had just passed SB 8, one of the country’s most restrictive abortion bills until Roe v. Wade was overturned the following year. As she contemplated bringing The Hunting Wives to life, Cutter saw the political stakes come into focus as well.

“I started thinking about the ‘red state, blue state’ of it,” she tells Vanity Fair ahead of the show’s season two premiere on Thursday. “What if…we really play this culture war?”.

“I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes,” claims showrunner Rebecca Cutter. “I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.”.

Sources indicate that the result was one of Netflix’s biggest breakout hits in recent years, sent up in a Saturday Night Live sketch as the “straight but lesbian, horny Republican murder drama.” As a show, Hunting Wives amps up the noirish aspects of the suspense thriller written by May Cobb, a native of the East Texas Piney Woods, and adds a heaping dose of MAGA-adjacent camp. Cutter finishes the mix with plenty of sex scenes, particularly between Malin Akerman’s Margo, a femme fatale partly inspired by Melania Trump who is married to a Republican gubernatorial hopeful, and Brittany Snow’s Sophie, a liberal do-gooder who, like Cutter, arrives in town from a blue corner of Massachusetts. (Cutter was raised in Cambridge and graduated from Wesleyan University, the Connecticut liberal arts college known for its progressive politics and pipeline to Hollywood.).

It has been revealed that hunting Wives executive producer Erwin Stoff told Cutter he’d pay for her to go to Texas to meet Cobb and breathe the Piney Woods air herself. She met Cobb’s father and her best friend from high school. She shot skeet with the women—she even got it in three, just as Sophie does in the first season. At a high-end Dallas shopping area where the likes of Gucci can be found, Cutter got a better sense of the hair, clothes, and bodies of her eventual characters. “I understand the notion that Sophie could be amused and entertained and intrigued by these women,” Cutter says, “and eventually seduced.”.

According to recent reports, cutter thinks of the show primarily in terms of its tonal mash-up: “I think we managed to wrangle it into one piece of art,” she says, “but there’s comedy, there’s violence, there’s noir, there’s soap, there’s earnest emotion.” To the extent that she assigned any political beliefs to the rich white women of Cobb’s novel, it was in the spirit of grounding her characters in the specifics of their world. Still, as we speak, Cutter decides “to get real with it.”.

Cutter on set. She describes Sophie, a fellow native of blue Massachusetts, as a surrogate for her own awakening to MAGA Texas.

Sources indicate that “The whole thing was a little bit of a parable, in my mind, of how you could fall for someone like [Donald] Trump,” she admits. “Sophie has her principles, but they only go so far. They end right where something starts to make her feel good.” Cutter was as curious as anyone else from her educated milieu about the quirkier aspects of Trump, like the Diet Coke button he had installed on the Resolute Desk. How liberating must it feel to embrace a movement so openly untethered from the pieties of politics and taste?

“Not that my show is a deep dive on Trump,” Cutter claims, “but maybe there is an element that’s sort of looking under the hood.”.

The twisted love story between Margo and Sophie entangles all of the wealthy, hard-drinking, gun-toting women in their orbit, and its central killing—one of several propelling the show forward, with a third season slated to begin filming this year—stems from an effort to cover up Margo’s abortion as her NRA-loving husband plots his political ascent. (In this proudly oversexed town, he has his own share of affairs.) Hunting Wives is the rare Netflix soap to receive steady coverage from mainstream national outlets; the fascination undoubtedly has something to do with the impression that, like Yellowstone or Morgan Wallen before it, the show unlocks something about MAGA’s cultural staying power. In a Latest York Times guest essay this month that evaluated the post-2024 Hollywood landscape, Sharon Waxman, the editor in chief of The Wrap, wrote, “From Melania on Amazon’s streaming service to The Hunting Wives on Netflix to the ever-expanding Taylor Sheridan universe on Paramount+ to Bari Weiss’s being put in charge of CBS News, the vibe shift was visible on all our screens.”.

Margo and her politically ambitious husband are partners in subterfuge and debauchery.

Recent findings suggest that cutter notes she had no particular agenda nor any “ultra-evil villain plan of how it was going to be received or how it would be culturally relevant.” But Hunting Wives is sprinkled with enough proper nouns—a Peter Thiel mention here, a Walmart reference there—and distinctly modern aesthetics that she can acknowledge its appeal as something of a Rosetta stone for the moment in MAGA femininity. Even in the ostensibly waning days of the movement, the plastic surgery and soaring heels continue to captivate and horrify coastal elites. Cutter says that Callie (Jaime Ray Newman), another of Margo’s lovers, has a bit of Kristi Noem and Marjorie Taylor Greene in her: that “sort of slightly butch, real gun, real ‘back the blue’ [element]…the toughness of those women.”.

The second season of Hunting Wives maintains the slipperiness that keeps the show from veering into moralism; it stands apart from other Trump-era art in its refusal to take sides. “I think I remember, in the pitch, someone saying, ‘But will red-state people like it too?’” Cutter recalls. “I was like, ‘I think so.’” Both Margo and Sophie are awash in their respective red and blue stereotypes, but neither is more admirable than the other. Their sordid union is a testament to the flexibility of both their principles and their preferences. From one vantage, it is, in the end, all about sex.

It has been revealed that “Margo is the symbol of freedom and sexuality and feminine power and empoweredness and selfishness that [Sophie] feels she’s lost,” Cutter says, adding that Akerman’s comfort in such a role helped drive her liberal use of physical intimacy. “The audience may disagree with me,” she says, but “I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes. I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.” Last year, though, when Netflix acquired Hunting Wives, which was initially ordered by Starz in 2023, Cutter had a more practical concern.

“I literally googled,” she recalls, “‘Does Netflix show boobs?’”.

Apple touts that the Apple Watch Series 12 delivers “the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable.” In fact, the organization conducted a study of more than 1,000 participants that found the Series 12 “achieved statistically better overall accuracy than every competing wearable it tested across workouts and daily activities.”.

Industry observers note that with the fresh system, Apple Watch Series 12 captures your heart rate every five seconds. Previous Apple Watch models, including the Apple Watch SE 3, take measurements every five minutes. The new Health Sensing System also enables a new readiness score feature, which factors in your recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score.

In a recent development, as I wrote in my review, the Apple Watch Series 12 brings some of the biggest improvements to Apple Watch health tracking in years. The fresh sensing system unlocks a trove of new data along with better accuracy.

Industry observers note that the Apple Watch lineup is incredibly strong right now. Whether you’re deciding between the SE 3 and Series 12, both offer great health tracking, battery life, and connectivity. The Apple Watch SE 3 is an excellent choice for people new to the Apple Watch ecosystem.

According to recent reports, the Apple Watch Series 12, however, is the best Apple Watch for most people. There are major improvements to the health tracking capabilities, offering meaningful steps forward in what the Apple Watch can tell you about yourself. In the two months I’ve had mine, I’ve come to appreciate the more frequent heart rate measurement and readiness score.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title.
  • EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title.
  • According to recent reports, motson, who passed way in 2023, previously provided commentary for EA's FIFA series, appearing in the game's first iteration in 1996 and featuring until 2005.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title. Motson, who passed way in 2023, previously provided commentary for EA's FIFA series, appearing in the game's first iteration in 1996 and featuring until 2005. According to the BBC, EA approached Motson's wife and son for permission to regenerate his voice and use his likeness for this year's entry in the series. Both agreed to the idea, but neither party has disclosed how much EA has paid for the use. Fred Motson, John's son, stated that he believed his father would've approved of this use of AI. "My dad was the least technological person in the world," Fred stated. "Till his dying day, he had a typewriter on his desk. So I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically, but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects." Peter Caulfield, founder of Save Our Voices Now, which campaigns against this exact use of AI, questions whether a family should be able to provide consent for someone who can no longer give it themselves. "If someone has signed a deal allowing their likeness to be used after they die, I have no issue with that," he explained. "But in life or in death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed. Being a family member shouldn't automatically give you that right either." This isn't upcoming to video games, either. Epic Games used a similar method to bring back the late James Earl Jones' voice for its Star Wars event in Fortnite, with the actor's estate agreeing to the use. It allowed players to converse with the AI bot while playing, and was very rapidly removed after some users managed to get the bot to spew out racist or vulgar phrases, all delivered with the voice of Jones. It also drew the ire of SAG-AFTRA, which claimed that Epic had violated labor practices. Derek Rae, one of the currently employed commentators on EA Sports FC 27, said he was excited by the inclusion of Motson's voice, and that he didn't believe AI was yet going to replace his own work on the game. When asked whether he would make the same decision to have his work endure for years to come through AI, he replied, "I'm hopefully many years away from having to make a decision like that.".

EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title.

According to recent reports, motson, who passed way in 2023, previously provided commentary for EA's FIFA series, appearing in the game's first iteration in 1996 and featuring until 2005. According to the BBC, EA approached Motson's wife and son for permission to regenerate his voice and use his likeness for this year's entry in the series. Both agreed to the idea, but neither party has disclosed how much EA has paid for the use. Fred Motson, John's son, stated that he believed his father would've approved of this use of AI.

"My dad was the least technological person in the world," Fred stated. "Till his dying day, he had a typewriter on his desk. So I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically, but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects.".

It has been revealed that peter Caulfield, founder of Save Our Voices Now, which campaigns against this exact use of AI, questions whether a family should be able to provide consent for someone who can no longer give it themselves. "If someone has signed a deal allowing their likeness to be used after they die, I have no issue with that," he explained. "But in life or in death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed. Being a family member shouldn't automatically give you that right either.".

In a recent development, this isn't new to video games, either. Epic Games used a similar method to bring back the late James Earl Jones' voice for its Star Wars event in Fortnite, with the actor's estate agreeing to the use. It allowed players to converse with the AI bot while playing, and was very quickly removed after some owners managed to get the bot to spew out racist or vulgar phrases, all delivered with the voice of Jones. It also drew the ire of SAG-AFTRA, which claimed that Epic had violated labor practices.

Derek Rae, one of the currently employed commentators on EA Sports FC 27, said he was excited by the inclusion of Motson's voice, and that he didn't believe AI was yet going to replace his own work on the game. When asked whether he would make the same decision to have his work endure for years to come through AI, he replied, "I'm hopefully many years away from having to make a decision like that.".

Virgin River will look a little different when it returns for season 8 in the wake of multiple cast exits.

Executive producer Richard Keith teased several latest additions — starting with Mitchell Slaggert, who has been cast as a new EMT.

In a recent development, “He’s brought on as part of the new hospital integration, and so he and a new doctor, Astrid, who’s played by Natasha Calis, come into town, and I think it’s just a nice chance to see Mel sort of get to empathize with how maybe Doc felt when she first came to town,” Keith told Swooon on Thursday, November 26. “Mel is the hometown girl, and there’s a new girl on the block. Mitchell is just such a breath of fresh air as a performer. He’s really sweet and really present and really fun, and it’s a nice new energy to bring to the cast.”.

Keith also confirmed that Austin Nichols would be back as Mel’s doctor ex.

“Austin’s wonderful on the show, and I think his relationship with Jack and Mel is complicated and really interesting to see how it unfolds and how it brings complications,” executive producer Erin Cardillo teased before Keith added, “I think, in a good way, it plays out in an unexpected way. It’s not the standard somebody’s ex comes back into the picture, right?”.

He continued: “Because of their son and all of the extenuating circumstances and the hopeful nature of Virgin River, the story takes some unexpected paths, which is cool.”.

Based on Robyn Carr’s book series, Virgin River follows the lives of residents living in a small town in Northern California, including Mel (Alexandra Breckenridge) and Jack (Martin Henderson).

The hit series, which premiered in 2019, also stars Colin Lawrence, Annette O’Toole, Tim Matheson, Benjamin Hollingsworth, Sarah Dugdale, Zibby Allen and Kai Bradbury.

In a recent development, after seven seasons, there have been some major departures from the Netflix show. Grayson Gurnsey left as Ricky after season 4, and Mark Ghanimé, who played Cameron, had a surprising exit once season 6 was released.

Recent findings suggest that “I think this season saw a little bit of a sendoff for Cameron,” showrunner Patrick Sean Smith exclusively told Us in December 2024. “In terms of Mark, the actor who I adore, he unfortunately won’t be coming back for season 7.”.

Smith didn’t rule out a potential return for the character in the future. “But that’s not to say that Cameron’s not a part of our world forever,” he added. “I would love to bring him back, and bring his character back when the story presents itself.”.

In March 2025, Virgin River returned for season 7, and it was later confirmed that Marco Grazzini will not reprise his role as Mike.

In another twist, Lauren Hammersley, who has played Charmaine since the show premiered, is also not expected to come back for season 8.

In a recent development, while you can find plenty of deals on older headphone models during Black Friday sales, it’s rare to see a record-low price and a nearly 30% discount on newer, highly rated models from top brands. That’s exactly why this deal on the critically praised Beats 360 headphones should be on your radar. They’re now down to $249 (originally $349.99) in Amazon’s early Black Friday sale.

According to recent reports, with a design that looks like the love child of the AirPods Max and the Beats Studio Pro, these have an adjustable telescoping frame and a unique modular design that lets you mix and match ear pad colors. The color-swapping bundle isn’t at the moment on sale, but it’s reassuring to know you can replace the ear pads as they wear out.

They’re controlled by two buttons on each earcup and powered by a dedicated Beats chip, with support for both Android devices and iPhones. You can switch noise modes and, on an iPhone, activate features like Personalized Spatial Audio in Settings. They last up to 32 hours with ANC on, which is longer than both the more expensive Sony WH-1000XM6 and AirPods Max 2.

It has been revealed that according to Beats, the 360 offer up to 1.75 times the noise cancellation of the Beats Studio Pro. PCMag’s review, which gave the headphones an “Excellent” rating, was impressed by how well they blocked out everything from plane engine noise to café chatter. The noise cancellation falls short of pricier models, and PCMag found the Sony WH-1000XM4C slightly better in that respect.

The PCMag review notes the headphones deliver “nice, deep bass, reasonably crisp highs, and a more neutral tuning than you might expect for a pair of Beats headphones.” If you’re after long battery life, rich audio, and plush earcups you can swap for a pop of color, $249 is a great price for the Beats 360 headphones.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in 2019, Danny Boyle, who was originally named the director for the James Bond film that eventually became No Time to Die, suggested Robert Pattinson as the man to take over as the next person to play Bond. Now, seven years later, that prediction has come true, as Pattinson was officially named the next 007 last week. Boyle isn’t done making suggestions, however, but now he’s switched to who should play the villain: Jack O’Connell.

In an interview on Alchemy with Anthony Mason, while promoting his latest movie Ink, Mason brought up Boyle’s prognostication, and Boyle took it one step further, saying:.

Recent findings suggest that but we have an actor in [Ink], Jack O'Connell, [who] would have been a great Bond, as well. And now I can see that in all this talk, they're talking about Jack O'Connell as a possible villain. They have that thing you want to watch them. And it's impossible to quantify what it is. Otherwise, we’d all buy it for ourselves.

Sources indicate that O’Connell was one of the (many) actors who were rumored to be in the running for Bond 26 before Amazon MGM and director Denis Villeneuve ultimately decided to go with Pattinson, and I think his take on O’Connell as the villain is also an inspired idea as well. Along with who could be the next “Bond Girl,” the next Bond Villain is another major casting chip that still needs to fall soon before filming kicks off, hopefully in 2027.

Sources indicate that O’Connell isn’t the only name being bandied about to play James Bond’s next villain. Another actor who has worked with Boyle before, Cillian Murphy, has been a popular choice among fans. Barry Keoghan, who worked with Murphy on the 2026 movie schedule in Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man (which was headed up by Bond 26 writer Steven Knight), is also a top pick. Idris Elba, whom many hoped (including me) could be the next Bond, though even he admitted he’s too old for the role now, is also a common name thrown out there (and honestly, maybe my pick).

It has been revealed that last week, after the Pattinson announcement, Brad Pitt even tossed his own name into the ring for the role. Now that would be an interesting choice! The latest rumors also point to Tom Hardy as the next villain, which would set up an interesting dynamic between the current Batman (Pattinson) and a former Batman villain (Hardy played Bane in The Dark Knight Rises).

There are still quite a few casting announcements for Bond 26 to look forward to, like M, Q, and Moneypenny, in addition to the villain, maybe a henchman or two, and, of course, the next Bond Girl. Oh, and who could possibly be in line to do the next Bond theme? It’s an exciting time to be a Bond fan. Meanwhile, Ink will be available to watch with a Netflix subscription on January 8th, after a short stint in theaters starting on December 11.

Industry observers note that upcoming York City is no stranger to bad weather, be it blazing-hot summers, snow-packed winters, or fierce windstorms. Unfortunately for countless families who have made it a holiday tradition to turn on the TV and watch giant totems of pop culture sail in the streets of the great city, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been officially delayed due to a forecast of rain and windstorms--a first in its 100-year history. In recent years, gaming icons have become more and more prominent during the parade. Beginning in 1993, a balloon of Sonic the Hedgehog marked the first game character to float among the procession. Since then, more characters have joined the festivities, including Mario, Pac-Man, Pikachu, and even Red the Angry Bird, among others. However, those who have followed the history of Macy's balloons know that the mix of bad weather and massive, floating objects can result in genuine danger for balloon handlers, bystanders, and objects on the streets. Rather infamously, Sonic's 1993 appearance was marred by an incident where the balloon got stuck on a lamppost, popping the balloon and injuring two bystanders. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DmTC0m7wQbs Other balloon bursts have proved even more catastrophic, with a series of mishaps in 1997 leading to a Cat in the Hat balloon causing injuries that left a woman comatose for days. Since then, more emphasis has rightfully been put on safety. While it might be disappointing to not be able to point at the TV and go "Mario!" with your younger cousins around the TV tomorrow, the balloons will get a chance to fly on Saturday starting at 8:30 AM ET, when the weather is likely to be significantly less awful. You can find other ways to fill the time--but maybe ask your relatives first if it's okay to let the kiddos watch you play GTA 6. Image credit: Getty Images / Craig T Fruchtman.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic is launching a new tool for builders called Claude Ship. The new AI feature allows Claude to “review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows.”.

Sources indicate that claude Ship is a latest product created especially for builders who code with agents. The idea is to make handling pull requests as automated as agentic coding.

“That’s why we built Claude Ship, available today in beta,” Anthropic says. “It can review PRs, fix them, and decide what’s ready to merge based on policies each team sets. Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person. The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

Claude Ship is comprised of three agents: Code Review, PR Steward, and Claude Approvals.

“Together, they take a pull request through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually,” Anthropic notes.

“Developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests with the upcoming /ship command in Claude Code,” Anthropic notes.

In a recent development, you can learn much more about Claude Ship here. Additional documentation can be found here.

Industry observers note that no matter what you do in GTA 6, it pales in comparison to being a Furry in that game. Anyone looking to externalize their inner animal spirit is in danger of being hunted, and you'll find out for yourself just how much the fictional state of Leonida hates Furries when you're given the chance to save one of them from being murdered by the cops. Should you help them? Absolutely, if you want an easy payday or a new weapon for your arsenal. How to find Chase the Fox Like several other missions in GTA 6, helping out the Furry resistance appears to trigger randomly. The mission takes place after Chapter 3, on Miramar Drive in Crosstown, Vice City, and you'll want to be cruising around that area at night, between midnight and 4 AM. Once it starts, you'll see cops pull up to hunt down a Furry by the name of Chase, and if you drive up to him, you can either give him a lift or leave him to his brutal fate. Outrun the cops If you do choose to help Chase, then get ready to be hunted down by cops. You'll pick up a three-star Wanted level, which means the cops will be in mildly hot pursuit of your vehicle. Reach the parking garage Chase will direct you to a nearby parking garage, where his Furry allies are waiting. After a short standoff, they'll welcome you into their ranks as an honorary Furry. Courier the group to safety To get the law off your polyester tail, one of your new allies will take your car and use it to distract the cops. Get inside the van, and you can bring the other Furries home to their swanky pad in Starfish Island. While you're driving, the Furries will interact with each other, and you can watch their hijinks. Choose your reward Once Chase and his pals are back home, you'll be offered one of two rewards: $15,000 in cash or the unique Furry DW-9 submachine gun. Personally, I'd go with the gun since it's easy enough to make cash in GTA 6, and having more weapons is never a bad idea. You'll also gain safehouse access to the Furry group's hideout, where you can stock up on weapons and body armor. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

Industry News: Sell Thy Neighbor: Trump Official Howard Lutnick and the Clandestine Deal to Sell NYC’s Glamorous Pierre Hotel
